en-120: lightburn provides a material testing function. you can perform a material test before processing a specific material to achieve the parameters you want. please refer to this video: lightburn material test card | onelaser xrf desktop if you don’t want to create the parameter test file yourself, you can also download the test file we have prepared. please note that due to ongoing lightburn version updates, there may be file mismatches or loss of details.
en-121: what is lightburn software? lightburn is professional laser control software that allows you to design, edit, and send jobs directly to your laser machine. it combines design tools with machine control, making it suitable for both beginners and advanced users. with lightburn, you can: design vector graphics and layouts adjust laser parameters such as power and speed preview jobs before running send files directly to the laser cutter lightburn is widely used across hobby, business, and industrial laser workflows. how the license works a lightburn license is a digital key used to unlock the software for permanent use. every new license comes with a year of free updates from the date you first activate it. after a year, you'll still be able to use any version of lightburn released before your license expired, but you'll need to renew your key in order to continue receiving updates for another year. if you renew before your key expires, you'll receive an additional two months on your one-year renewal. a lightburn license automatically comes with 3 seats, meaning you can activate it on three computers at one time. you can use the lightburn license portal to view and remove activations on your key, freeing up activations in use on old or inoperable computers so you can activate on new ones. quick start follow these links step by step, and you'll be able to get started quickly. before watch the video, you must know the info about the 1laser: the origin for 1laser is rear left. it's controller is ruida install instruction connecting lightburn via ethernet installing lightburn on macos lightburn setup & first job toolbar click toolbar instruction to learn more. user interface and features click user interface and features to learn more. more info about lightburn lightburn provides a professional and complete knowledge base that covers all the features and operation guides of the software. if you need a deeper understanding, you can refer to lightburn kb . lightburn also has many video instructions, click lightburn youtube to learn more. thank you for your patience. if you still have any questions, please don't hesitate to ask. we are always here to help.
en-122: laser head without red dot indication is a troubleshooting guide designed to help users diagnose and resolve issues where the red dot indicator does not appear during machine operation. this page explains common causes, inspection steps, and electrical checks to determine whether the issue lies with the red light module, optical components, or control board. issue phenomenon: during the operation of the device, no red dot indication is found. operation guide: 1. check whether the red light is operating normally use an m2 hexagonal wrench to remove the hexagonal nut on the back cover of the laser device and remove the back cover. find the red light indicator mounting socket and check whether the red light indicator is working properly (is there a red light?) red light is normal: the reflector may be oxidized or dirty, preventing red light reflection. clean and maintain the optical lens. abnormal red light: please follow the steps below to troubleshoot. 2. red dot indicator interface contact is bad find the red light indicator adapter interface and check whether it has poor contact. note: the red light indicator adapter interface is located on the back cover of the laser. use an m2 hexagonal wrench to remove the hexagonal nut on the right door of the device and remove the right door of the device. find the energy-saving control panel shown below. remove the wires as indicated, then use a multimeter set to dc 5v to measure the output voltage. normal voltage: if the voltage is 5v, the red light indicator is faulty. please contact onelaser support for replacement. abnormal voltage: if the voltage is not 5v, the tl energy-saving control motherboard is faulty. please contact onelaser support for replacement.
en-118: this guide explains how to export design files stored in a onelaser machine’s internal memory back to your computer. it covers supported software options, connection methods, file formats, and important limitations to ensure successful file transfer and reuse. preparation hardware: your onelaser machine and your computer (windows pc recommended). software: rdworks, makerboost, or lightburn. operation connecting the computer and the machine you can connect the machine via usb or network (ethernet/wi-fi). once connected, open either rdworks or makerboost on your pc. note: lightburn does not support exporting files stored in the machine’s memory. rdworksv8 download link: click here makerboost (beta) download link: click here exporting or running files using rdworks after the software successfully connects to the machine: locate the doc tab in the property bar on the right side and select the file you wish to export. click upload to save the file as an .rd file onto your pc. important: while rdworks allows you to open .rd files, please note that parsing these files may occasionally result in distorted lines or layout issues. .rd files can be directly run and processed via rdworks. exporting or running files using makerboost after activating the trial and successfully connecting to the machine: navigate to file > device file management in the top left corner and select the file you wish to export. click export to save the file as a .tl file onto your pc. important: .tl files cannot be opened for viewing within the software, but they can be directly run and processed via makerboost. opening or running files using lightburn lightburn cannot export files from the machine's memory. it does allow you to open .rd files. important: please be aware that lightburn’s parsing of .rd files may result in line distortion or errors. once opened, .rd files can be directly run and processed through lightburn. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis.
en-87: this article provides an overview of common alarm messages that may appear on the one laser touchscreen interface. these alerts are designed to protect the machine, ensure operational stability, and assist users in identifying potential risks during laser processing. because the device firmware is continually updated, users may occasionally encounter pop-up messages not yet included in this guide. 1. x- or y-axis boundary exceeded overview the machine will issue an “out-of-bounds” alarm when the design file extends beyond the physical working limits of the device. for example, the x series model provides a processing area of 600 × 300 mm . when either axis exceeds this range, the system interrupts job execution to prevent mechanical collision or excessive travel. why this happens this alert commonly arises from: a design file larger than the available workspace incorrect origin selection that shifts the design outside the valid working area misalignment caused by offsetting the starting point too close to an edge in the reference diagram provided with the machine,the yellow region represents the machine’s working boundary,the green square indicates the user-defined origin,and the blue/gray areas denote the file’s placement. if the origin is selected incorrectly—such as the example where it is set near the edge—the file may partially fall outside the allowable range, triggering the alarm. recommended actions verify that the design dimensions fall within the permitted workspace. reset the origin and ensure that the entire file lies safely within the machine’s processing area. 2. insufficient buffer distance overview during engraving, the laser head requires a certain amount of buffer space to accelerate, decelerate, and execute rapid directional changes. if the file is positioned too close to the boundary of the working area, the machine may detect insufficient buffer distance and trigger a warning. why this happens this alert is typically caused by: a file placed extremely close to the workspace edges an origin location that does not leave the head enough space for motion planning recommended actions adjust the origin to give the design additional margin from the machine’s physical limits. re-run the job once sufficient buffer distance has been ensured. 3. water protection trigger (xt series) overview the xt series utilizes a glass co₂ laser tube paired with a water-cooling system . to protect the tube from overheating, the machine incorporates a water-flow sensor. when this sensor fails to detect water movement at the beginning of a job, the system displays a water-protection alarm. this prevents tube damage and ensures long-term operational safety. inspection point to access the water-cooling components, open the rear housing using an m2 screwdriver. recommended actions confirm that the water pump’s signal cable is properly connected. check whether the water pump is operating normally and providing consistent flow. 4. combined alarm window (door cover protection / flame alarm / water temperature alarm) several safety-related alerts share a common pop-up interface. when this window appears, users should assess the possible causes one by one. 4.1 door cover protection overview for safety reasons, the device requires all doors and covers to remain fully closed during operation. if any cover is open or not securely latched, the system issues a door-protection alarm and stops the job. recommended action: ensure that all covers and access panels are completely closed before restarting the process. 4.2 water temperature alarm overview when the water temperature inside the cooling tank exceeds 45 °c , the machine automatically halts operation and emits a beeping sound. this prevents thermal damage to the laser tube, which is sensitive to elevated temperatures. recommended action: wait until the water temperature falls back to a safe range before resuming work. 4.3 flame alarm overview the system includes a flame-detection sensor that monitors for abnormal combustion events within the workspace. if the sensor detects a flame or receives an irregular signal, the machine will stop immediately for safety. diagnostic steps inspect the flame-detection probe to ensure it is not bent or obstructed, and verify that all wiring is intact. open the right-side panel (remove the cover with a screwdriver). locate the intelligent control board and disconnect the in6 interface. restart the machine: if the beeping alarm persists even after in6 is disconnected, the control board may have malfunctioned and should be evaluated by technical support.
en-117: this guide explains how to properly adjust the air pipe securing screw on x-series laser machines. it outlines when adjustment is necessary, required tools, and step-by-step instructions to restore airflow while preventing damage to the air pipe. caution the screw securing the air pipe is calibrated to its optimal state before leaving the factory. do not tighten it unnecessarily , as this may crush the pipe and cut off the airflow. only adjust this screw if there is no airflow during processing. preparation x-series machine m2 hex wrench flat-head screwdriver operation remove the laser head covers you will need to remove both the front and right-side covers of the laser head. front cover: the front cover is magnetic; pull it off directly. right-side cover: use the 2 mm hex wrench to remove the securing screws. adjust the air pipe securing screw locate the air pipe adjustment screw as shown below. use a flat-head screwdriver to perform the adjustment: clockwise: tightens the screw. counter-clockwise: loosens the screw. important: if the screw is too loose, it may fall out during operation. if it is too tight, airflow may be restricted or completely blocked. adjust until the pipe is secure while maintaining proper airflow. reassembly once the adjustment is complete, reinstall the right-side cover with the screws and snap the magnetic front cover back into place. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis.
en-114: this page explains how to diagnose and resolve issues when an axis driver indicator light turns red and flashes. it covers what the flashing patterns mean, why the driver enters protection mode, and how to safely restore normal machine operation. problem description remove the right-side cover panel to locate the axis drivers. under normal operating conditions, the status indicator light on the driver should be solid green. if the red indicator light begins to flash, it indicates an abnormality with the driver or motor position. cause&solution please refer to the table for the corresponding questions and solutions. red light flashes protection function cause solution 1 flash overcurrent / short circuit a short circuit or wiring error has occurred in the motor or driver, triggering overcurrent protection. power off the equipment, inspect the motor wiring for the corresponding axis, and then power the equipment back on. 2 flashes overvoltage protection the driver enters protection mode when the voltage exceeds 40 v dc. power the equipment off and then back on. if this occurs frequently, consider slightly reducing the input power supply voltage. 4 flashes phase loss protection the driver was powered on without a motor connected, or there is a current imbalance, excessive current, or motor coil overheating. power off the equipment, inspect the motor wiring for the corresponding axis, replug the connectors, and power back on. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-26: problem description engraving result in blurry effects or "ghosting" (double images). cause the scanning offset parameters tested at the factory were not written to the machine from lightburn after the machine was received. vibrations during shipping and logistics may have caused a slight deviation. solution every machine is shipped from the factory with a dedicated scanning offset settings parameter card (as shown in the image below). after connecting your computer to the machine, open device settings and click basic settings to find the scanning offset adjust . enter the values from your parameter card. important reminders: the values on the card are in mm/s . using other units, such as inch/s, will lead to incorrect scanning offset results. ensure that your software is set to the correct unit: mm/s. click write and then click read to confirm that the parameters have been successfully stored in the machine. before closing the window, ensure that scanning offset adjustment is enabled. for dual-source machines, you must enter the specific parameters for both laser1 and laser2 separately. due to vibrations during shipping and transport, the factory-set parameters may become slightly misaligned. we recommend validating the precision by performing a test engraving after entering the initial parameters: draw a rectangle on your workspace. set the layer mode to fill . double-click the layer to enter the settings window. set the speed to a corresponding value from your parameter card (e.g., 400 mm/s, 800 mm/s, or 1200 mm/s) and apply an appropriate power setting. set the line interval to 0.5 mm. observe the test result, as shown in the image below. if the ends of the even-numbered scan lines finish further to the right than the odd-numbered lines, you should slightly increase the line shift value. if the even-numbered lines finish further to the left, you should slightly decrease the line shift value. note: the adjustment range is very small, typically from 0.001 to 0.01 (e.g., changing 0.150 to 0.155). you may need to repeatedly test and adjust until the ends of the even-numbered and odd-numbered scan lines are perfectly aligned. once the adjustment is complete, you can export and save the scanning offset settings file . this allows you to directly import the configured parameter file if you ever connect a new computer to this machine for processing. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-109: this page provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for resolving stuttering, abnormal noise, or jamming issues when the z-axis platform moves up or down. it outlines common symptoms, root causes, and step-by-step corrective actions to restore normal z-axis operation. problem description stuttering or abnormal noise occurs when moving the z-axis up or down. the platform stalls at a specific height and cannot move further upward. physical resistance or strange sounds are noticed when manually pulling the z-axis belt. cause alignment issues: one of the z-axis lead screws is not perfectly vertical or parallel. driver settings: incorrect dip switch positions on the z-axis driver. parameter errors: incorrect factory parameter settings in the software. solution method 1. inspect and align the z-axis lead screws this issue typically occurs in new machines or after a significant physical impact that causes the lead screws to bend or shift out of vertical alignment. open the front bottom door panel and check the four lead screws for any visible bending. to ensure the lead screws are parallel, measure the distance between the lead screws as shown in the diagram (sides a, b, and c). to measure side b, you must first remove the metal protective plate. the lengths of sides with the same color (e.g. all a sides, all b sides, all c sides) should be identical. it is normal for sides b and sides c to have different values. measure from the edge of one lead screw base to the edge of the opposite lead screw base. if you find a side with an inconsistent length, loosen the two screws on the black base, slightly adjust the position until the measurements match, and then retighten the screws. method 2. check the z-axis driver dip switches open the bottom door panel on the right side of the machine. locate the z-axis driver (usually positioned toward the top left). ensure that only switches 2, 3, and 7 are in the on (pressed down) position. all other switches must be in the off position. method 3. verify factory parameters open lightburn and navigate to machine settings. then locate the z axis settings section. check if your parameters match the standard values (see reference image). if the values do not match, please contact the onelaser after-sales team to obtain the correct parameter values. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-113: this guide explains how to troubleshoot and adjust the camera when recognition accuracy is low on onelaser machines. it focuses on resolving common issues such as missing red dot indication and ensuring clear, accurate camera operation. problem description during the operation of the device, no red dot indication is found. solution method 1. check if the lens is contaminated use a dust-free cloth and cleaning fluid to clean the lens. method 2. re-import the calibration file in the lightburn software, click “window” and “camera control” to enable the camera control function. select the camera name, usually “k35a2361” . note: please check the camera screen to ensure that the camera is correctly selected and connected. right-click “save settings” and select “import camera settings” . the camera calibration file is located on the random usb flash drive. please insert the usb flash drive into the computer and select the corresponding folder according to the device model. after importing the camera calibration file, click “save settings” to save the settings. method 3. exposure adjustment the camera may cause unclear images due to exposure issues, thus affecting the accuracy of camera recognition. you can adjust the appropriate exposure to enhance the camera's recognition clarity. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-104: connecting the onelaser hydra to lightburn via wi-fi allows stable, cable-free operation. by correctly setting the module mode, ip address, and lightburn device configuration, users can ensure reliable communication and smoother workflow without usb limitations. checking the module status step 1. open the bottom right door panel of the hydra machine to locate the switch module shown in the illustration. step 2. confirm if the button 1 is currently pressed on the switch: when button 1 is pressed, the wi-fi module is engaged, allowing for wi-fi connectivity. when button 2 is pressed, the lan port mode is engaged, allowing for external ethernet connectivity. step 3. start the machine and confirm that the vonets module is powered on. connecting to the machine's hotspot step 1. locate the hydra's hotspot module in your computer's wi-fi connection list. name: hydra + hotspot + the last five digits of the serial number （e.g. hydra hotspot 8a2b4） default password: 12345678 step 2. based on the hotspot's default ip address, you must change the controller board's ip address accordingly. the hotspot's default ip subnet is 192.168.254.xxx. set hydra's ip address within 192.168.254.xxx. important: when entering the ip address on the hydra control panel, the xxx part of 192.168.254.xxx must not duplicate the ip address of the hotspot or any other machine on the network. mac：open wifi settings, view network details and locate ip address. win：open command prompt, type ipconfig and check the ipv4 address. how to modifying hydra ip address? the hydra hotspot does not support internet access . after connecting, your computer will be unable to access the internet. to enable basic internet functionality while connected, we will provide instructions on how to bridge the connection to an upstream router (the user's normal internet-enabled wi-fi). once the initial configuration is complete, the computer can subsequently connect to the hydra directly through the user's usual wi-fi network. bridging to an upstream router step 1. connect your computer normally to the hydra's hotspot module. name: hydra + hotspot + the last five digits of the serial number （e.g. hydra hotspot 8a2b4） default password: 12345678 important: during the bridging process, you must only be connected to the hydra's hotspot module. do not connect to any other wi-fi or network. step 2. open your browser and enter 192.168.254.254 (or http://vonets.cfg). step 3. enter the username and password, then click wizard . username: admin password: admin step 4. click scan hotspots and select your upstream wi-fi. step 5. enter the wi-fi password, check disable hotspot , and click apply . step 6. click reboot to apply the settings. step 7. connect to hydra through the upstream wi-fi and verify the new ip address. connecting the machine in lightburn step 1. open lightburn and click devices → create manually . step 2. enter the correct ip address during setup. step 3. the setup and connection are now complete. troubleshooting 1. cannot connect to hydra while on bridged wi-fi? enable wi-fi 4/5 compatibility if using a wi-fi 6 router. 2. computer cannot access the internet? reduce distance between the computer and the upstream router. 3. restore vonets module to factory settings hold the reset button for 5 seconds after power-on. important reminder: if the issue persists, please submit a support ticket for further assistance.
en-66: problem description the starting and ending points of the cut product are misaligned or do not close accurately . the edges of the lines exhibit slight waviness or vibration patterns . cause the belts on the x-axis or y-axis is either too loose or adjusted too tightly . solution important note: when adjusting the belts, it is crucial to achieve a moderate tension. belts that are either too loose or too tight on any part of the machine will negatively affect performance. method 1. adjusting the y-axis drive belt as shown in the image below, loosen the three screws in group a to unlock the y-axis motor bracket. then, turn screw b to adjust the belt tension. once a moderate tension is achieved, re-tighten the three screws in group a . method 2. adjusting the x-axis drive belt as shown in the image below, loosen the three screws in group a to unlock the x-axis motor bracket. then, turn screw b to adjust the belt tension. once a moderate tension is achieved, re-tighten the three screws in group a . standard tension: when adjusting, the belt should be in a state of moderate tension. this can be assessed by the finger press test, which should allow for a slight movement margin of approximately 1 to 2 mm. over-tension assessment: if there is absolutely no movement when pressed, the belt is over-tightened and must be loosened slightly. final check after adjustment, manually push the laser head to slide it along the x and y directions, observing for any sticking or abnormal noise . rerun a test job and check if the starting point and ending point misalignment issue is resolved. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-98: problem description the laser head has dropped along the z-axis and cannot be raised using the up button, remaining at its lowest position. upon restarting the equipment, the laser head homes to the top-left corner, but the z-axis position of the laser head does not reset. cause the white plastic component on the right side inside the laser head has detached from the lead screw. solution turn off the machine and remove the cover of the laser head. locate the detached white component on the right side inside the laser head. slowly push the white component upwards until it re-engages with the lead screw. it does not need to be pushed all the way to the top. restart the machine and check if the laser head successfully resets in the z-axis direction. press the z-axis up button on the control panel to check if the movement of the laser head in the z-axis has returned to normal. if movement still fails: check for any loose wires inside and around the laser head. if any can be securely plugged back in, do so. if the wires cannot be secured or if the issue persists, report the damage to official after-sales personnel for further troubleshooting guidance or warranty action. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-96: problem description the camera's accuracy is low, resulting in an unclear image when capturing the workspace. the camera is capable of achieving a resolution of approximately 2560×1920 in its native camera software, but in lightburn, it is limited to 1920×1080. the highest available resolution cannot be accessed. when capturing an image on the canvas, only a low-resolution image is obtained, which prevents effective outline extraction. resolution comparison example cause the camera lens is dirty. the camera parameters in lightburn are inappropriate. incorrect camera settings within the lightburn software. solution clean the camera lens please check if the lens is dirty and use a dust-free cloth and cleaning solution to clean the camera lens. adjust exposure parameters exposure issues can cause the image to be blurry, which negatively affects the accuracy of the camera's recognition. adjust the exposure parameters appropriately to improve the clarity of the camera's recognition. modify camera settings lightburn indicates that this setting can only be modified on windows systems. click settings in lightburn and click camera option. locate the camera capture system option and then check the box for custom camera system. this will help lightburn enable the highest available resolution supported by the camera. 1.7.00 version 2.0.00 version important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-95: preparation offline programmer (model: mini-pro) supporting software for the programmer： /firmware-upgrade-2/supporting_software.exe update program file (must be specific to your machine series) procedure importing the program to the programmer (using a computer) use the provided usb cable to connect the programmer to your computer. the light on the programmer should illuminate. open the supporting software on your computer (ensure you select the correct programmer model). configure the options according to the settings shown in the screenshot below. click add and select the update program file for your machine. click export , then the programmer will emit a tone when the export is complete. importing the program to the board locate the tl-timer board inside your machine. connect the programmer's probes to the corresponding metal holes on the board (pay attention to the orientation of the probes). the light on the programmer should illuminate. press the button on the programmer. the light will flash when the process is complete. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-88: problem description when processing material using the pass-through door, the material is thick, and the laser head already contacts the material surface, making correct focusing impossible. cause the material is too thick. the maximum thickness allowed through the pass-through door is approximately 20 mm. the lower part of the lens barrel is too long. solution method 1. use thinner material note: the thickest material that can be processed using the pass-through door is approximately 20 mm (about 0.78 inches). method 2. remove the cone tip loosen the screw indicated by the arrow and remove the lens barrel. unscrew the cone tip from the bottom of the lens barrel (this will not affect the auto-focus function ). reinstall the lens barrel back into its original position. note ①: push the lens barrel upwards until the rubber ring on the barrel reaches the aperture. note ②: check that the screw is tightened, otherwise the lens barrel may fall out during the next job, causing damage. important: after you finish using the pass-through door, remember to restore the lens barrel to its original configuration before returning to normal processing mode. method 3. shorten the lens barrel's length loosen the screw indicated by the arrow and remove the lens barrel. then, pull the rubber ring on the lens barrel down. reinstall the lens barrel, pushing it further up than its usual installation position. continue until you feel the upper edge of the lens barrel is stopped, then tighten the screw. important: after you finish using the pass-through door, remember to restore the lens barrel to its original configuration before returning to normal processing mode. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-89: 3m adhesive protective gloves beam combiner mount and lens m3 hex wrench recommended adhesive brand procedure assembling the beam combiner put on the protective gloves. apply a tiny amount of 3m adhesive to the positions indicated by the arrows on the mount. observe the arrow marking on the side of the beam combiner lens. place the lens into the beam combiner mount with the arrow pointing downwards. ensure the lens lies flat in the frame. check that no squeezed-out glue has contaminated the lens or the mount surface. allow it to sit undisturbed for a period until the adhesive is firmly set. replacing the beam combiner use the m3 hex wrench to loosen the four screws indicated by the arrows on the beam combiner bracket. remove the old beam combiner and place the new, assembled beam combiner into the exact same position. finally, retighten the screws securely. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-73: problem description the air pump does not run (no air is blowing) when the equipment is executing a processing job. cause air assist is not enabled in the software's layer settings. the air hose inside the laser head is damaged or leaking. the soft tubing connected to the air pump is disconnected or damaged. the connector between the air pump and the mainboard is loose. the wiring harness between the mainboard and the air pump is internally burned out or broken. the air pump itself is damaged. the mainboard itself is damaged. solution method 1. check software settings check the layer settings section in your laser software to ensure air (blowing) is enabled for the current process. lightburn makerboost method 2. check air hose open the laser head and check the internal tubing for any signs of damage or leaks . source: image provided by a customer check the tubing connected to the air pump for any signs of misconnection, disconnection, or damage . note on misconnection: this refers to connecting the tubing to the external air pump channel when using the built-in pump, or vice-versa. built-in air pump external air pump method 3. check circuitry and air pump open the right side panel of the machine to locate the mainboard (as shown in the illustration below). toggle the switch indicated by the red arrow to the m position (the furthest right position) to force the pump on. check if the air pump starts working, and simultaneously observe if the light indicated by the yellow arrow turns on. if the pump fails to start after toggling the switch: prepare a multimeter. first, check if the wire connectors shown in the illustration below are firmly seated. next, use the multimeter probes to test the voltage of the wires between the mainboard and the air pump (as shown in the illustration). the voltage should be able to reach 24v (minor fluctuations are normal). if the voltage reaches 24v but the air pump does not work: the preliminary diagnosis is that the air pump is damaged and needs replacement. if the voltage measurement significantly deviates from 24v: the preliminary suspicion is an internal wiring issue or a mainboard failure . important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-75: after installing the air assist kit, both of the test buttons are permanently lit (on) without being pressed, and the airflow cannot be adjusted using the control knob. the installation wiring has been checked and appears to be correct. cause the air assist system has not been properly switched from standard mode to intelligent mode . solution adjust the mode open the machine's control panel menu . select external device to enter the configuration page. check whether the current status is set to standard mode . if it is, switch the setting to intelligent mode . check mainboard switch position open the right side panel of the x-series or hydra-series machine. locate the mainboard shown in the illustration below. check if the switch at the position indicated by the red arrow is currently set to the m position (the furthest right position). if it is set to the m position, switch it back to the furthest left position. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-71: preparation before installation dust protection kit linear rail limit plate pan head screw m3 × 6 2 mm hex wrench and 2.5 mm hex wrench installation procedure use the 2 mm hex wrench to loosen the fixed screws on the back of the laser head, allowing the top cover to be opened smoothly. use the 2 mm hex wrench to loosen the two fixed screws on the cable trough sheet metal. remove the originally damaged part. properly slot the part a of the dust protection kit around the air tube cable, then secure it onto the cable trough sheet metal and tighten the screws. refer to the illustrated position and use the 2.5 mm hex wrench to loosen the screws located inside the laser head. use the 2 mm hex wrench to remove the three screws on the right cover plate of the laser head, and carefully remove the right cover plate. remove the originally damaged part. take out the part b of the dust protection kit. feed the cable through the left hole, then push the dust protection kit component completely into position, ensuring the dust cover is securely installed onto the lead screw. tighten the screws inside the laser head and reinstall the right cover plate. restore the top cover plate to its original position and tighten its fixed screws. locate the installation position for the linear rail limit plate on the back of the laser head. use the 2 mm hex wrench to secure the pan head m3 × 6 screw. installation is complete. check that all components are securely fastened and correctly positioned. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-53: hydra 7 hydra 9 hydra 13 hydra 16 this manual has been designated as the onelaser hydra serial machine installation and user guide; the manual is divided into five chapters, including general information instructions, safety instructions, the key components of every laser cutting systems and the installation steps, operation instructions and maintenance instructions from onelaser. first, it should be emphasized that the installation of each system must meet the requirements, and make it consistent with the installation requirements of onelaser. if not, the machine will not working properly，poor performance, life shortened, maintenance costs increased and even machine damage . the note is for getting a specific requirement of system installation, and we hope every customer try to understand these notes before installation and usage, thus you can correctly install and use. if you meet any installation problems, you can contact our technical staff and customer service staff. chapter 1. general chapter 2. safety chapter 3. process of installing chapter 4. operation chapter 5. maintenance
en-65: problem description when a square is drawn on the workspace canvas, the actual processed graphic has a deviation in its width and height dimensions (e.g., a square becomes a rectangle). cause the step distance coefficient of the stepper motors is inaccurate. solution calibrating via lightburn machine settings connect to the device. draw a square on the canvas, such as a 50×50mm square (or equivalent size in inches). start the job and then measure the actual width and height of the processed graphic. click machine settings in lightburn. navigate to calibration axis. select the x axis, and input the measured values into the corresponding fields for requested distance (e.g. 50mm) and actual distance (the measured value). the software will automatically calculate the new step distance coefficient. click write to save the new setting to the machine. repeat the same steps for the y axis. you may need to perform this calibration one or more times to obtain the most accurate parameters. calibrating via makerboost vendor settings connect to the device. click settings → vendor setting and enter the password: tl9501. click calibrate xy step in the bottom-right corner of the window. in the new window, input the cutting power and click the cutting button. the device will automatically cut a square. measure the actual width and height of the processed square. input these values into the corresponding fields. the software will automatically calculate the new step distance coefficient. you may need to perform this calibration one or more times to obtain more accurate parameters. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

manifests as the kerf widening , the cut becoming gradually shallower , or the laser failing to cut through the material entirely. when checking beam alignment by moving the laser head to the four corners of the workbed, the burn marks left on the tape do not coincide . cause beam path misalignment can be caused by many factors, including: the angle of a mirror mount was accidentally shifted during the cleaning of the mirrors. shipping and vibration caused the optics to shift out of alignment. solution use an m2 hex wrench to remove the front door cover, back door cover, and left side en-61: problem description when the machine is connected using lightburn, the device executes the cutting layer first, regardless of its position in the layer list. this can cause the workpiece to be blown out of place, leading to cutting errors. cause the optimization setting for job processing order is not enabled. tabs were not added to the profile designated for the cutting process. solution optimize job processing order open the optimization settings window in your processing panel. ensure that the enable optimization and output re-ordering switch is turned on . ensure that order by layer is prioritized (set at the top of the list). then, place the cutting layer at the end of the layer sequence in your layers panel. you may refer to the functions in the additional options section of the image above for more in-depth processing optimization. add tabs to the cutting layer profiles adding tabs prevents the finished piece from falling out and shifting during the job. manually add tabs: select the add tabs tool from the left toolbar. click on the graphics where you want to add the tabs. automatically add tabs: double-click the layer to open the cut settings editor window. turn on the tabs / bridges switch. this allows you to automatically set tabs on the graphics. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-60: problem description when connecting the machine to the computer using the usb cable, the computer emits the connection notification sound, but lightburn is unable to locate the device when searching. when checking the device manager , the connected usb device is visible, but attempts to update driver fail. cause the ftdi d2xx driver is not installed. solution navigate to the official ftdi website ( https://ftdichip.com/cn/drivers/d2xx-drivers/ ) to download the d2xx driver . be sure to select the correct version based on your computer's operating system version and cpu architecture. install the d2xx driver program. once the driver is installed, the computer should correctly recognize the machine, and lightburn should be able to connect successfully. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-52: problem description regardless of the position on the workbed, the processing results in the far areas (further away from the origin) are consistently worse than those in the near areas. this manifests as the kerf widening , the cut becoming gradually shallower , or the laser failing to cut through the material entirely. when checking beam alignment by moving the laser head to the four corners of the workbed, the burn marks left on the tape do not coincide . cause beam path misalignment can be caused by many factors, including: the angle of a mirror mount was accidentally shifted during the cleaning of the mirrors. shipping and vibration caused the optics to shift out of alignment. solution 1.remove access panels: detach the three panels on the left side of the hydra unit (as illustrated) to provide access for viewing and adjusting the beam path. 2.system preparation: navigate to the "alignment" interface on the hydra touchscreen. set the laser power to approximately 25% . warning: the "pulse" button will be used to emit laser light for beam location verification. when activating "pulse", ensure no part of the human body is in, or can cross, the beam path. 3.beam path and mirror identification: the laser beam path and the corresponding mirror assemblies are identified in the figure below: method 1. adjusting optical path a 1. remove the focusing lens and place a piece of double-sided tape on the base. press “pulse” and check the burn mark. if the mark is off-center, adjust screws a/b (vertical) or c/d (horizontal) using a 3 mm hex wrench . repeat until the burn mark is centered. 2. reinstall the focusing lens and place tape at optical mirror 1 . pulse again and adjust if needed. important: press two adhesive sides of tape together first to avoid contaminating the lens. method 2. adjusting optical paths b & c important: in optical path c, optical mirror 3 and optical mirror 4 are shared by the 70w rf tube and the glass tube and should not be adjusted . adjust only optical mirror 1 and optical mirror 2 . optical mirror 1 & optical mirror 2 (fine-adjustment method) 1. apply tape over the through-hole on optical mirror 2 . pulse and adjust via optical mirror 1 knobs. optical mirror 1 knob guide rotary knob 1: clockwise → shifts burn mark right counterclockwise → shifts burn mark left rotary knob 2: clockwise → shifts burn mark inward counterclockwise → shifts burn mark outward 2. apply tape to optical mirror 3 and the red-light port. adjust optical mirror 2 knobs until the burn mark is centered. optical mirror 2 knob guide rotary knob 1: clockwise → shifts burn mark down counterclockwise → shifts burn mark up rotary knob 2: clockwise → burn mark moves left counterclockwise → burn mark moves right 3. apply tape on optical mirror 4 . move the laser head to upper-left and bottom-left . the marks must overlap. adjusting only optical mirror 1 (simplified method) 1. apply tape on optical mirror 4 . pulse and adjust optical mirror 1 knobs until centered. optical mirror 1 knob guide rotary knob 1: clockwise → burn mark moves up counterclockwise → burn mark moves down rotary knob 2: clockwise → burn mark moves right counterclockwise → burn mark moves left 2. apply new tape on optical mirror 4 . move to upper-left and bottom-left corners. verify marks overlap. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-50: problem description cutting: the cut line appears wide and thick. the machine cannot cut through the material with standard parameters. the bottom edge of the material is not cut cleanly. severe burn marks, charring and potentially flaming occur. engraving: engraved edges are blurry. the material exhibits fraying or rough edges. cause the auto-focus function was not used before processing began. the focus distance value pre-set at the factory has been altered. the material surface is uneven or warped. the focus lens is installed incorrectly (e.g., loosely mounted or installed beneath the lens holder). the focus lens or mirror optics are dirty. the laser beam path is misaligned. solution always remember to use the " auto-focus " function before starting a job to set the focal distance to the correct value. enter the machine settings window, locate the focus distance parameter, and check if the value is set to 1.5 (or the correct default value for your machine). if the material is uneven, use magnets or clamps to press down on the four corners of the material. remove the cover of the laser head. take out the focus lens holder and check if the lens is loose or installed beneath the lens holder. use the focus lens removal tool or a thin steel ruler to gently tighten the lens or reinstall it above the lens holder . be extremely careful not to scratch the lens itself. use the cleaner and cotton swabs found in your toolbox to clean the optics. affix tape to the outside of the third mirror mount on the laser head. move the laser head to the four corners of the workbed (e.g., top-left, bottom-left, etc.), and tap the pulse button on the control panel at each corner. observe if the four burn marks are consistent and centered. if they are not consistent, you must re-align the beam path . important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-51: problem discription when the laser head is processing in a specific area of the work zone, the cut line widens and carbonization occur. however, processing results in all other areas of the workbed are normal. cause if the issue becomes progressively worse the further the laser moves to the right: this could be due to beam path misalignment or an unlevel working platform . if the issue primarily appears on the left side: this is most likely caused by an unlevel working platform . solution step 1. check and level the working platform check the distance between the cone tip and the working platform at various points. if the distance from the cone tip to the platform is inconsistent in the problematic area compared to other areas, the working platform is unlevel. remove the honeycomb panel. you will see two metal bars (front and back) that hold the knife-edge slats; each bar has five screws. loosen the screws located beneath the area where the processing/distance measurement issue occurred. use your hand to slightly lift or push down the metal bar to finely adjust the horizontal angle of the entire working platform. after the adjustment, be sure to tighten the screws and reinstall the honeycomb panel. step 2. check for beam path misalignment place tape on the mirror mount at the laser head. move the laser head to the four corners of the working platform ( top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right ). then, tap the pulse button on the control panel at each corner to leave a burn mark on the tape. observe whether the four burn marks overlap and are centered. if the burn marks do not overlap, it indicates beam path misalignment, and you will need to calibrate the laser path. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-49: problem description during a vector cutting operation, multiple cut lines appear instead of a single, clean line. cause multiple laser beam paths or scattering issues. this commonly occurs after the laser head sustains an impact or after an optical component in the beam path becomes misaligned: slight angular deviation in the angle of a mirror. the entire laser head assembly is askew. the focus lens is slightly loose or tilted. solution 1. check if the focus lens is loose. if it is, use the focus lens removal tool (which you can search for and purchase on amazon) or a thin steel ruler to gently tighten the lens . be extremely careful not to scratch the lens itself. 2. place a piece of tape on the third mirror mount of the laser head. move the laser head to the four corner positions of the working plane ( top-left, bottom-left, top-right, and bottom-right ), and at each position, tap the pulse icon on the control panel. observe the burn marks left on the tape. if the burn marks are not consistent or are off-center, you need to re-align the entire beam path. if the burn marks are centered but the shape of the spot is abnormal, check the focus lens and the nozzle for contamination or damage. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-48: problem description flaming occurs at the point where the laser exits the nozzle during processing. cause & solution category 1: new or recently used machine issues causes symptoms solutions insufficient air assist flow flaming, charred edges, and excessive smoke in the cut line. increase the air pressure. check the air tube for blockages or leaks. use an external air compressor or air pump. regularly clean the nozzle and check that air is blowing out. ensure air assist is enabled in the software. incorrect focus charring, wide cut line, and flaming. use the auto-focus function before starting the job. material flammability occurs when processing inherently flammable materials (e.g., mdf, bamboo, wood, density board). increase the air assist flow. increase the cutting speed. poor exhaust system efficiency excessive smoke generation, or even the appearance of flames. check the exhaust pipes and fan/blower for clear passage. check the exhaust pipes and fan/blower for clear passage. connect an external exhaust fan. category 2: issues due to machine/component aging causes symptoms solutions exhaust fan deterioration hot smoke cannot be extracted in time, leading to secondary combustion (flare-ups). clean the fan impeller blades and ducting. replace the exhaust fan or connect an external exhaust fan. air pump or compressor aging insufficient air assist pressure, resulting in flames not being blown away. replace the air pump or air compressor. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-25: xrf model xt model 38w rf metal tube laser for sharp, precise engraving with long lifespan and instant startup, ideal for detailed work. 55w co₂ glass tube laser for powerful cutting on thicker materials — an affordable, high-performance choice. this manual has been designated as the onelaser x serial machine installation and user guide; the manual is divided into five chapters, including general information instructions, safety instructions, the key components of every laser cutting systems and the installation steps, operation instructions and maintenance instructions from onelaser kraft engineering crop. first, it should be emphasized that the installation of each system must meet the requirements, and make it consistent with the installation requirements of onelaser kraft engineering crop. if not, the machine will not working properly, poor performance, life shortened, maintenance costs increased and even machine damage. the note is for getting a specific requirement of system installation, and we hope every customer try to understand these notes before installation and usage, thus you can correctly install and use. if you meet any installation problems, you can contact our technical staff and customer service staff. chapter 1. general chapter 2. safety chapter 3. process of installing chapter 4. operation chapter 5. maintenance
en-43: problem description after updating lightburn to version 2.0, using the camera function prompts a message requiring a full camera re-calibration via the calibration wizard. this step is mandatory, even if a camera calibration file was previously imported in version 1.7. however, when following the wizard and attempting to capture images, the display shows a black screen, blank screen, or garbled image. cause lightburn version 2.0 updated the camera function and rewrote the driver. the issue may occur because the software is using an old-version camera calibration profile within the new version 2.0 environment. solution based on testing, the first time you switch from lightburn 1.7 to 2.0, you can bypass the calibration wizard by directly importing the correct settings: in the camera window, right-click and select " import camera settings. " import the calibration configuration file found on the usb drive that came with your machine. by following this method, you can successfully use the camera function in lightburn 2.0 without having to go through the mandatory calibration wizard that causes the display error. important reminder 1: please note that whether you are switching from a new version back to an old version (downgrade) or from an old version to a new version (upgrade), you may encounter the black screen, blank screen, or similar issues during the image capture step. in this situation, you can simply import the correct calibration configuration file to use the camera function normally, entirely bypassing the need to enter the calibration wizard. continue using this method until lightburn officially fixes this bug. important reminder 2: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-33: problem description after switching from the rotary axis back to regular cutting mode, the machine cannot properly reset, the x and y axes move at excessive speed, and the head hits the limits without stopping. solution turn the rotary switch on on the machine and power on the machine. wait for approximately one minute until the main page appears on the control panel. open lightburn (or your laser software) and connect to the machine. open the rotary setup window and disable the " enable rotary " option. turn the rotary switch off on the machine. finally, press the " reset " button on the control panel. the machine should now be able to reset and return to normal cutting operation. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-35: problem description the red dot pointer beam is not collinear with the actual laser beam path. cause the red dot pointer system was not re-aligned after the main laser beam path was adjusted. solution use an m2 hex wrench to remove the machine's back cover and left side cover (remove the corresponding screws at the arrow positions indicated in the image). please secure and store these screws. apply a piece of double-sided tape onto the third mirror mount. on the control panel, navigate to "laser setting." set the parameters to cw, 5 ms, and 30% power. then, tap the pulse icon on the home page to leave a burn mark on the tape. locate the red dot indicator on the machine. use an m3 hex wrench to adjust the three screws on the mirror mount to align the red dot position. 1. screw a: adjusts the red dot horizontally (left/right movement). turning clockwise moves the red dot path to the right; turning counter-clockwise moves the red dot path to the left. 2. screw b: adjusts the red dot path diagonally to the upper-right and lower-left. turning clockwise moves the red dot path to the lower-left; turning counter-clockwise moves the red dot path to the upper-right. 3. screw c: adjusts the red dot path diagonally to the upper-left and lower-right. turning clockwise moves the red dot path to the upper-left; turning counter-clockwise moves the red dot path to the lower-right. adjust the red dot position until it perfectly overlaps with the burn mark left by the main laser beam. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-28: problem description the control panel is displayed in chinese. solution to change the language setting, follow these steps: tap the menu icon on the navigation bar to access the menu page. on the menu page, tap the second icon labeled " 语言 " to open the language settings. select the " english " option. tap " 确定 " at the bottom of the page. the language of the interface will now be switched to english. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-216: introduction for years, laser manufacturers have competed by advertising higher and higher engraving speeds. 600mm/s. 800mm/s. 1200mm/s. but experienced users quickly discover an important reality: a machine that moves fast is not necessarily a machine that engraves well. many laser systems begin to lose detail, introduce vibration artifacts, create blurry edges, or produce inconsistent results once speed increases. that is because real high-speed engraving is not only about motion speed — it is about maintaining precision under extreme acceleration. the cobra series was designed specifically to solve this problem. with up to 1200mm/s engraving speed, 2g acceleration, and high-detail 800 dpi output, cobra focuses not only on speed itself, but on stable high-speed production quality. why faster laser engraving often produces worse results when engraving at high speed, the laser head constantly changes direction. every corner, curve, and small detail introduces: inertia frame vibration belt oscillation delayed laser response motion overshoot on lower-end laser machines, these problems become obvious very quickly. common symptoms include: blurry text jagged edges double-shadow engraving distorted circles loss of fine detail this is why many machines can technically “reach” high speed, but cannot maintain clean engraving quality during real production work. the real key to high-speed engraving: acceleration many buyers only compare maximum speed specifications. in reality, acceleration is often far more important. why? because most engraving jobs involve constant direction changes. small graphics, logos, photographs, and text require the laser head to repeatedly: start stop reverse direction reposition a machine with poor acceleration spends most of its time slowing down instead of engraving efficiently. this is where cobra’s 2g acceleration becomes critical. higher acceleration allows the machine to: maintain productivity on complex designs reduce corner distortion improve detail consistency increase real-world throughput especially in production environments, acceleration matters more than theoretical top speed. why high-speed co₂ systems are difficult to engineer achieving stable high-speed engraving on a co₂ laser machine is significantly harder than many people realize. unlike diode systems, glass tube co₂ machines must manage: optical alignment stability frame rigidity motion synchronization vibration control high-speed beam consistency at high speed, even small structural weaknesses become amplified. this is why many budget co₂ laser machines advertise high speeds but struggle during long production runs. the challenge is not simply moving faster. the challenge is maintaining optical precision while moving faster. how cobra maintains precision at high speed the cobra series was engineered around stable high-speed operation. key performance features include: up to 1200mm/s engraving speed 2g acceleration system fine-detail 800 dpi engraving clean edge optimization stable motion structure this combination allows cobra to maintain detail quality even during demanding production tasks. typical applications include: batch wood signage engraving acrylic photo engraving leather logo production personalized gift manufacturing small business batch processing instead of sacrificing quality for speed, cobra is designed to deliver both. who benefits most from high-speed laser engraving? high-speed engraving is especially valuable for: etsy sellers custom gift businesses small production workshops personalized product brands batch engraving services higher engraving efficiency can directly reduce: production time cost per item delivery delays operator workload for many businesses, faster and more stable engraving directly improves profitability. conclusion high-speed engraving is not simply about how fast the laser head moves. it is about whether the entire motion system, frame structure, and optical design can maintain precision under high acceleration. that is the difference between machines that only advertise speed — and machines designed for real production. the cobra series was built for users who need both productivity and engraving quality.
en-217: introduction one of the most common questions in the laser industry is: “can a co₂ laser engrave metal?” the short answer is: not effectively on bare metal. this limitation has led many users to explore dual-laser systems that combine co₂ and infrared technology in one machine. the reason is simple: different materials respond differently to different laser wavelengths. a dual-laser system dramatically expands the range of materials and applications a single machine can handle. the cobra platform was designed with this flexibility in mind. why standard co₂ lasers struggle with bare metal traditional co₂ lasers operate at a wavelength of approximately 10.6μm. most bare metals reflect a large portion of this wavelength instead of absorbing it efficiently. as a result: energy transfer becomes inefficient engraving quality becomes inconsistent surface marking is often weak this is why many “metal engraving” demonstrations on co₂ lasers are actually engraving: painted surfaces powder coatings anodized layers spray-coated marking compounds the laser is often interacting with the coating — not the raw metal itself. why infrared lasers work better on metal infrared laser modules use shorter wavelengths that are absorbed more efficiently by metals. this allows: more concentrated energy transfer cleaner metal marking higher contrast engraving reduced thermal spread infrared systems are particularly effective for: stainless steel aluminum titanium coated metals metal business cards metal tags and nameplates this makes ir technology ideal for detailed metal engraving applications. the biggest advantage of a dual-laser system the true value of a dual-laser machine is versatility. instead of owning separate machines for different materials, users can process a much wider range of products within a single platform. typical applications include: wood cutting acrylic cutting leather engraving metal logo engraving personalized gifts industrial labeling product branding for many small businesses, this flexibility opens entirely new revenue opportunities. why more workshops are choosing dual-laser solutions small workshops and creators increasingly prefer dual-laser systems because they help reduce: equipment cost workspace usage workflow complexity learning curve instead of switching between multiple machines, operators can handle more material types within a single production environment. this is especially valuable for: etsy businesses custom gift makers startup workshops small-scale production studios multi-material product brands cobra’s infrared expansion module the cobra platform supports optional infrared laser expansion for users who require broader material compatibility. this allows users to combine: co₂ en-218: introduction many beginners assume poor engraving results are caused by incorrect power or speed settings. in reality, one of the most common causes of failed laser projects is incorrect focus. even small focus errors can dramatically affect: engraving sharpness cutting efficiency edge quality burn marks material consistency this is why auto-focus systems have become increasingly important in modern laser machines. the cobra series was designed to simplify this process for both beginners and production users. why laser focus matters so much a laser beam only reaches maximum energy density at its focal point. when focus is correct: the beam spot becomes smaller energy concentration increases engraving becomes sharper cutting becomes cleaner when focus is incorrect, common problems include: excessive burning yellow edges blurry engraving incomplete cuts thick engraving lines even high-powered lasers cannot compensate for poor focus positioning. why manual focusing is difficult for beginners manual focusing sounds simple, but real-world usage introduces many variables. users must constantly account for: different material thicknesses uneven surfaces lens focal lengths material warping operator inconsistency this is one of the biggest reasons new users experience failed engraving attempts. often, the issue is not the laser settings themselves — it is inconsistent focal distance. how auto-focus systems work an auto-focus system automatically adjusts the laser head height to maintain the correct focal distance. this helps eliminate human error and improves production consistency. key advantages include: faster setup reduced adjustment mistakes improved repeatability better batch consistency easier material switching for production workflows, auto-focus can significantly improve efficiency. why red dot positioning is also important in addition to auto-focus, red dot positioning helps users preview the laser path before processing. this improves: material alignment logo placement batch positioning multi-piece layout accuracy for small products and custom engraving work, accurate positioning can greatly reduce wasted materials. cobra’s user-friendly focus system the cobra series combines multiple features designed to simplify focusing and positioning: auto-focus functionality red dot positioning integrated laser head design magnetic quick-swap focus setup these features help users: reduce material waste improve engraving consistency speed up workflow simplify machine operation this makes cobra especially suitable for: beginners small businesses personalized product makers batch engraving workflows conclusion laser engraving is not difficult because the technology itself is complicated. in many cases, the real challenge is maintaining accurate and repeatable focus. auto-focus systems help reduce human error, improve consistency, and make laser production significantly more accessible for both beginners and professional users. for users who value workflow simplicity and reliable results, cobra’s auto-focus system provides a practical production advantage.

en-22: learn how to properly connect and set up the air purifier for your x series machine , including installation, power connection, and airflow adjustment for optimal performance. 1. preparation consumable preparation: one laser x model device x 1 air purifier x 1 phillips screwdriver x 1 debug software: none 2. operation step step 1. install the equipment air duct to the air inlet of the purifier use a cross screwdriver to tighten the hose clamp. step 2. connect the purifier to the power supply step 3. turn on the power of the purifier, start the purifier, and adjust the air volume to the highest.
en-23: follow this step-by-step guide to unbox, set up, and prepare your onelaser x series for its first use, ensuring safe and smooth operation. unbox steps step 1: cut cable tie. step 2: after removing the carton packaging, you can move the machine to your workbench. step 3: remove the protective film. step 4: remove all items included and remove the inner foam. step 5: confirm all items. please refer to the items of the tool bag here → [tool bag included parts]. step 6: disassemble the back box and add distilled water to the water tank. if your equipment is xrf series, you can ignore steps 6–7. remove the screws using an m2.5 screwdriver and take off the rear box cover. please keep the removed screws. step 7: locate the water tank and use a funnel to add distilled or purified water. after the water filling is completed, please remember to install the rear cover back. step 8: installation of exhaust outlet. first, remove the screws on the plate. connect the 24v connector. install the exhaust outlet. step 9: install the exhaust pipe. step 10: connect the power cable, usb cable, and camera cable.
en-24: the riser base (base boost™) is a precision-engineered add-on for the onelaser x series that expands your machine’s versatility and workflow. designed for makers who work with taller objects like 40oz tumblers, bottles, or large décor pieces, the riser base elevates your laser to provide extra clearance height and straight-through pass access up to 160mm. beyond size flexibility, the base boost™ helps create a cleaner, dust-free, and safer workspace by improving air circulation and debris management. whether you’re engraving large products or running production batches, base boost™ ensures stability, precision, and efficiency—all in one sleek upgrade. understand the riser base assemble the riser base
en-47: configure computer step 1. connect the machine and computer with ethernet cable. step 2. go to start > control panel > network and sharing center, configure the connection for local connection. step 3. select properties. step 4. in the properties window, select use the following ip address. step 5. set the ip address to 192.168.1.30 and the subnet mask to 255.255.255.0. configure the laser software step 1. the first step is installing the lightburn software . run the lightburn installer install lightburn finish installing step 2. open lightburn and set a connection. step 3. select ruida, then click next. step 4. select ethernet/udp and continue. step 5. enter the default ip 192.168.1.100 to complete lightburn network configuration. step 6. name your laser and enter the work area — for x series, 600 × 300 mm. step 7. select rear left as the origin. step 8. the connection is finished. start your project the connection interface will display the laser status as “ready”, and now you can start your project. note: the ethernet connection is not plug and play and requires manual configuration. it does not work with lightburn’s “find my laser” feature. the laser uses a static ip that must match your network. default ip: 192.168.1.100 | subnet mask: 255.255.255.0.
en-105: connect your onelaser machine via wifi with this step-by-step guide. learn how to configure vonets wifi, set up lightburn, and ensure a stable connection. important info wifi connection only can communicate with controller, cannot connect the camera. wifi connection is not the most stable method. please choose according to the actual situation. operational guide connect the wifi turn on the machine. find the wifi "vonets_****", the default password is 12345678. configure the wifi 1. log in to http://vonets.cfg or 192.168.254.254 to configure parameters. account and password: admin 2. select the wifi that matches your computer network and click 'next'. 3. enter the wifi password, check 'disable hotspot,' and click 'apply'. 4. click 'to connect'. 5. click start connecting. 6. then it's connected. 7. click the 'reboot'. 8. open lightburn, click device. 9. create manually. 10. select ruida 11. select ethernet/udp 12. for onelaser, the default ip address is 192.168.1.100 13. name your laser and enter the work area, for x series, the area is 600×400mm. 14. select rear left as origin. 15. then the connection is finished. 16. back to the home page, select xt and if it’s show ready, it means the machine is connected. you can run a job.
en-106: learn how to connect your onelaser xt or xrf to lightburn via usb. follow this simple setup guide to install lightburn, configure ruida, set origin, and start engraving. operational guide 1. install the lightburn software, please see the link below to install: install the lightburn software 2. connect your computer and laser machine with a usb cable. 3. open lightburn and set a connection. 4. select ruida. 5. select serial/usb. 6. name your laser and enter the work area — for x series, the area is 600 × 300 mm. 7. set the rear left as origin. 8. then it's finish. 9. back to the home page and select xt. if it shows “ready,” it means the software is connected.
