en-111: the onelaser x series glossary provides a clear explanation of the main components found on onelaser x series laser engraving and cutting machines. this glossary helps users quickly understand the function of each part, supporting safe operation, troubleshooting, maintenance, and daily use. whether you are a beginner or an experienced operator, this reference makes it easier to identify machine components and understand their roles during laser cutting and engraving workflows. glossary table no. component description 1 camera used to check the working status of the processing area. 2 laser head the component from which the laser beam is emitted. 3 touch panel used to control the machine, including movement and running files. 4 pm2.5 detector detects temperature, humidity, and pm2.5 levels in the air. 5 function panel used to connect external devices and the power cable. 6 e-stop (emergency stop) rapidly cuts off the power supply to the equipment in an emergency. 7 cooling fan used to cool the rear cover of the machine. 8 exhaust vent used to connect the exhaust pipe.
en-271: problem description if you observe that the z-axis does not respond to the up/down controls or autofocus, but the laser head can still be moved manually by turning the z-axis screw, the z-axis stepper motor may require further inspection and replace the z-axis motor if necessary. this issue may indicate a fault in the z-axis stepper motor or one of its phase circuits. when the motor cannot operate normally, the z-axis controls and autofocus function may become unresponsive even though the z-axis mechanism itself can still be moved manually. cause a phase circuit of the z-axis stepper motor may have an open or intermittent connection, causing the stepper motor driver to report a phase error and preventing the z-axis from moving normally. solution if you have received the new z-axis motor (lead screw motor assembly), follow the steps below to install it: remove the top cover of the laser head by removing the two screws on the back. loosen the motor mounting bracket directly below the z-axis motor by removing the two screws on the back. locate the two screws above the left side of the z-axis motor. remove them to loosen the limit plate. turn the lead screw counterclockwise to gradually remove the motor from the top. turn the bottom of the motor upward to access the four mounting screws. remove these screws to separate the motor from the motor mounting bracket, then disconnect the corresponding connector. install the new z-axis motor by following the same steps in reverse, then reinstall the laser head housing. ⚠️ note: if there is not enough room to work comfortably, you can also remove the housing on the right side of the laser head. reinstall it in its original position after completing the replacement. remember to remove the honeycomb panel; otherwise, the z-axis travel will not be sufficient to remove the lead screw motor. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-273: problem description the machine wobbles or shakes during high-speed engraving, especially when engraving at speeds above 400 mm/s . the workbench may also shake noticeably during operation. cause at high engraving speeds, the rapid movement and direction changes of the laser head generate greater inertial forces. if the machine is placed on a lightweight, unstable, or flexible workbench, these forces can cause the machine and workbench to vibrate. solution make sure the machine is placed on a stable, level, and sturdy workbench . check that the machine is securely positioned and that the workbench does not move or shake easily. test the machine at a lower engraving speed. if the vibration is significantly reduced, the workbench stability is likely contributing to the issue. if necessary, increase the stability or weight of the workbench. if the machine continues to wobble on a stable workbench, check the belts, panels, and other mechanical components for looseness. note: some vibration at very high engraving speeds can be caused by machine inertia and does not necessarily indicate a machine fault. improving the stability of the workbench can significantly reduce the vibration. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-279: problem description during engraving or cutting, intermittent sparks or small flames may appear around the laser head or nozzle. brown or burnt residue may also be found around the nozzle or lens area. causes possible causes include: dust, smoke, or residue has accumulated around the laser head. the nozzle or lens area is contaminated. the air assist is not working properly. the material being processed produces excessive smoke or residue. the focus or material position is incorrect. solution stop the machine and allow the laser head to cool before inspection. check the nozzle and the area around the laser head for dust, smoke residue, or other contamination. clean the affected area according to the recommended laser head and lens cleaning procedure. check that the air assist is working properly and that the air hose is securely connected. check the material position and make sure the material is at the correct focus height. run a low-power test after cleaning to confirm whether the sparks or flames have disappeared. if sparks or flames continue to occur after cleaning and checking the air assist, stop using the machine and contact technical support for further inspection. note: do not continue engraving when abnormal flames or sparks are present. excessive residue around the laser head can affect engraving quality and may contaminate or damage optical components. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-90: preparation 2mm hex wrench 2.5mm hex wrench new magnet hinge procedure attention: during the process of replacing parts, please ensure that all disassembled screws are safely preserved to prevent loss, as this is crucial for the subsequent reinstallation. disconnect the machine's main power cord, exhaust duct, and any other connected components. separate the machine from the riser base ( this step requires two people to lift and move the machine ). then, remove the base. use a hex wrench to remove the screws on the right support panel (a total of 10 screws). separate the right support panel and the front and rear door covers from the riser base. use a hex wrench to loosen and remove the faulty magnet hinge that needs replacement. then, install the new magnet hinge and tighten its securing screws. reassemble the riser base. place the machine back onto the riser base, and reconnect the exhaust duct, power cord, and any other connected components to complete the replacement. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-145: when the width of elevator doors, room doors, or other passages is insufficient for the device to pass through, you can disassemble some of the outer shell components to reduce the width requirement for the device. preparation work personnel requirements: a minimum of 4 people are required to assist in the handling process, please arrange personnel accordingly. tool requirements: one laser hydra series device *1 hex wrench *1 masking tape *1 door cover key *1 scissors *1 disassembly requirements to facilitate subsequent handling and to reduce the weight of the device, we will disassemble components such as the device's door cover and processing platform. please ensure that these removed parts are kept safely. after the device and base are disassembled, the height is: height: 77.5cm (including the height of the emergency stop and key switch), width: 111cm. if the height of 77.5cm is still not enough to pass through, you will need to remove the emergency stop switch and key switch. after removal, the height will be: 75cm. remove the device door cover and scrap bin 1. use the key and hex wrench to remove the upper and lower front door covers of the device. 2. remove the scrap bin. dismantle the emergency stop switch and key switch note: the method for removing the emergency stop switch and key switch is the same; here, only the operation for removing the emergency stop is demonstrated. 1. locate the emergency stop switch, flick the yellow lock, unlock it, and then remove the lower half of the emergency stop switch. 2. counterclockwise rotate to unscrew the fixing ring and remove the upper half of the emergency stop switch. dismantle the honeycomb board and blade 1. lower the platform to a certain height, use scissors to cut the ties that fix the honeycomb board. 2. remove the honeycomb board and blade. note: when removing the honeycomb board, do not let it hit the laser head, as this may cause the optical path to deviate. 3. when closing the door cover, use masking tape to secure it and prevent the door cover from opening during transportation. separate the device from the base 1. the screws that fix the base are located inside the lower door cover on both the left and right sides of the device; you need to use the key to open the door cover. 2. use the hex wrench to remove the screws that fix the base, as shown in the figure. 3. at this point, you can separate the device from the base. after separation, move the device into the room. note: it is best to prepare a handcart before flipping, and flip the device onto the cart for easier subsequent handling. restore the device after the device is inside the room. 1. align the device with the base and tighten the fixing screws. 2. install the door cover, honeycomb board, key switch, and other accessories onto the device.
en-112: introduction this manual serves as a comprehensive resource for the installation, operation, and maintenance of the onelaser hydra gen 2 laser system . it details all necessary procedures, from initial setup to daily use and maintenance, with a strong emphasis on safety protocols. all users must read and understand this manual in its entirety prior to operating the system. why choose the hydra gen 2? the hydra gen 2 , the flagship model of the onelaser hydra series, is equipped with a dedicated, high-power, new generation co₂ rf laser source . it is designed for modern precision manufacturing and high-efficiency production, offering a powerful combination of exceptional processing quality, high speed, and versatile material handling. precision grayscale control: the wide 0–70w power range allows for master-level grayscale processing. it precisely renders intricate gradients, from subtle surface marks to deep engravings, delivering photo-realistic detail with stunning clarity. high-speed accuracy: powered by a new hybrid motion system and an ultra-fast modulation frequency, the hydra gen 2 guarantees pinpoint accuracy at speeds up to 2000 mm/s . this ensures sharp, high-resolution ( 2000 dpi ) output on complex graphics and fine text, dramatically increasing productivity. efficient power output: the dedicated 70w new generation co₂ rf laser source delivers more power where it is needed. this significantly increases material removal rates, enabling deeper and faster cutting of thick materials to reduce cycle times and maximize production efficiency. important notice for safe operation and optimal performance of your hydra machine, you must strictly follow all specifications and onelaser’s installation requirements. failure to do so could result in: reduced performance and poor results shortened machine lifespan higher maintenance costs serious machine damage potential safety hazards this manual provides the essential installation specifications. we strongly advise that all users read and fully understand every instruction and warning in this guide before installing or operating the machine. need help? if you encounter any issues during installation, contact our technical support team immediately. table of content chapter 1. general 1.1 safety information carefully read this entire document before installing and operating the machine. warning: failure to read, thoroughly understand, and strictly adhere to the instructions in this operation manual may result in serious personal injury, death, property damage, fire, electric shock, machine malfunction, degraded performance, reduced machine lifespan, or severe damage to the machine! the following symbols and notes are used to alert users to potential hazards and critical operational information. pay close attention: high voltage: there is a risk of electric shock. this device can only be maintained by professionals. laser radiation: this device has laser radiation function. please pay attention to the danger of laser beam. please avoid direct exposure of eyes or skin to laser during operation. be sure to follow the safe operating procedures to prevent personal injury or machine damage. fire hazard: high potential for fire. never run unattended! caution: 1.use only approved parts: when replacing machine components, only use the components or spare parts provided or listed in the associated parts list. the use of third-party components may lead to abnormal machine performance, increased safety risks, and will void the product warranty. 2.follow auxiliary machine instructions: auxiliary machine supplied with this device is accompanied by its own dedicated instruction manual. installation or operation of any auxiliary machine must strictly comply with the requirements specified in its respective manual. (contact us if you require related information). 1.2 compatible materials the hydra gen 2 offers exceptional material compatibility and is capable of processing a wide range of substrates: the laser can process a wide variety of materials such as rubber, acrylic, cork, cardboard, glass, leather, marble, various plastics, and wood. additionally, it supports engraving directly onto coated, painted, or anodized metal surfaces, significantly expanding its application scope. notice: this device has laser radiation function. please pay attention to the danger of laser beam. please avoid direct exposure of eyes or skin to laser during operation. be sure to follow the safe operating procedures to prevent personal injury or machine damage. 1.3 disposal suggestion do not dispose the machine with domestic waste! electronic devices have to be disposed according to the regional directives on electronic and electric waste disposal. in case of further questions, please ask your supplier. he might take care of proper disposal. 1.4 specifications while our 70w co2 rf laser source is primarily equipped on the hydra 7 and hydra 9 models for peak performance, we are happy to offer customized solutions. if you would like to have the 70w laser integrated into another hydra model, please contact us to discuss your specific needs. mechanics hydra 7 hydra 9 working area 700mm*500mm (27.56'' x 19.69'') 900mm*600mm (35.43'' x 23.62'') table size 790*590mm (31.10'' x 23.23'') 990*690mm (38.98'' x 27.17'') z axis height 225mm (8.85'') max work height 225mm (8.85'') max. speed 2000mm/s, @4g motor servo motor and step motor work piece table honey comb table max. table load 20kg 30kg net weight 175kg 311kg standard head 2.5” focus lens diameter 2.5”@ focal length 20mm@ diameter mirror diameter 25mm beam combiner diameter 20mm 25mm feed-through door design features a pass-through design allowing material to enter from the front and exit from the back. provided the material remains balanced and adequately supported during processing, there is theoretically no limit to the material length that can be handled. dimensions hydra 7 hydra 9 w x d x h 1300*1045*1035mm (51.18”x 41.14”x 40.
en-206: introduction in general, camera lenses are not perfectly flat, which leads to image distortion. this effect is especially noticeable with fisheye lenses used to capture large laser working areas (which is the case for onelaser machines). to ensure proper camera functionality, calibration is required to compensate for this distortion. although the calibration process takes some time, once completed, the calibration file can be exported and saved, eliminating the need for frequent recalibration. onelaser machines are preloaded with corresponding camera calibration files at the factory. you can find these files on the usb drive included with the machine and import them into lightburn for normal use. however, due to uncontrollable factors such as transportation, if the camera does not function properly after importing the file, please follow the methods below to recalibrate the camera. if you encounter any issues, contact onelaser official support. notes calibration and alignment are both essential for proper camera setup. each method includes two steps :calibration must be followed by alignment. please download the required calibration files (see lightburn official documentation for details): apriltags in pdf or lbrn2 format (recommended) calibrationcircles.png print the image and attach it to a rigid, flat surface such as cardboard, acrylic, or wood. method 1: calibrate camera lens + calibrate camera alignment 1. calibrate camera lens ensure the correct camera is selected in the camera control window. right-click and select “calibrate camera lens.” select the appropriate preset and choose the fisheye camera, then click “next.” the interface will update, showing a capture button and placement instructions. if you have not prepared the calibration pattern in advance, you can print it at this step. place the printed pattern according to the diagrams shown on screen. important: for shots near the edge of the camera view, position the pattern close to the edges (where distortion is strongest) to improve calibration accuracy. a lower score is better , as it represents lower average pixel error. if the capture fails or looks incorrect, do not worry—capture multiple times until a valid image is obtained. after calibration is complete, click “next” to proceed to alignment. 2. calibrate camera alignment prepare a material such as cardboard, wood, or acrylic to engrave the alignment pattern, and mark the center of the target. click “fit workspace” to scale the pattern to match the laser working area. set appropriate laser speed and power to produce a visible mark without cutting through the material. (settings vary depending on machine and material; the example shown is for thin wood.) run a “frame” preview to ensure correct positioning on the material. start engraving. if the marking is too light, adjust settings and repeat. once the pattern is clearly visible, click “next.” capture the alignment image. when all four targets are clearly visible, click “capture image.” mark each target by double-clicking its center. you may zoom or pan the image as needed. a red “+” marker will appear after each double-click.place markers in order ( 1, 2, 3, 4 ) at the center of each target. if a marker is misplaced, double-click near it to reposition or click “undo last” to remove it. place all markers as accurately as possible. click “next,” then “finish” to complete the process and save the results. 3. update overlay return to the workspace and click “update overlay” or press alt / option + c . this captures the camera view and overlays it onto your workspace. method 2: calibrate camera lens (labs) + calibrate camera alignment 1. calibrate camera lens (labs) download and print the apriltag calibration pattern , and mount it on a rigid, flat surface. in the camera control window, ensure the correct camera is selected. right-click and choose “calibrate camera lens with tag tracking (labs).” click “next.” a live camera feed will appear along with additional controls. the system will detect apriltags and overlay green squares on them. adjust the pattern position so that as many tags as possible are visible. note: if few or no tags are detected, adjust the camera focus. click “capture.” move and rotate the calibration pattern within the camera’s field of view, capturing images at different positions. the system will build three models: standard camera extended camera fisheye camera use the dropdown menu to compare results. the better model will show less distortion . you may also select “original calibration” for comparison. choose the model with the least distortion, then click “next.” if satisfied with the result, click “save.” 2. calibrate camera alignment return to the workspace. in the camera control window, right-click and select “calibrate camera alignment.” the steps are the same as in method 1 . 3. update overlay return to the workspace and click “update overlay” to project the camera view onto the workspace. notes based on internal testing, method 1 provides higher accuracy and is therefore recommended. this guide is based on the xrf model . due to the camera-to-platform distance, calibration was performed with the lid open and the board elevated. for hydra models , you can close the lid and place the board directly on the platform. camera calibration is sensitive to movement. even slight shaking can introduce errors. it is recommended to perform calibration with two people or use a stable fixture. although lightburn suggests an error below 0.5 is acceptable, this is near the upper tolerance limit. based on our testing, achieving an error below 0.2 will provide significantly better calibration results.
en-270: problem description when using a newer version of lightburn for unidirectional engraving or cutting, the processing position may become offset. the offset distance is usually close to the backlash compensation (line shift) value set for the processing speed of the current layer. in previous versions of lightburn, unidirectional engraving generally did not have this issue. after testing bidirectional engraving, the measured backlash value could simply be entered as line shift to compensate for the backlash during bidirectional engraving. however, after updating lightburn, using the original line offset setting may cause a position offset during unidirectional engraving or cutting. solution the current temporary workaround is as follows: record the current line shift value for the processing speed. delete the value in line shift or set it to 0 . enter the original line shift value into initial offset . run another unidirectional engraving / cutting test. for example: the line shift value is the backlash compensation value obtained from bidirectional engraving tests. moving this value to initial offset can temporarily resolve the position offset during unidirectional engraving / cutting in newer versions of lightburn. note this is currently a temporary workaround . the same parameter settings may not currently provide completely offset-free results for both unidirectional and bidirectional engraving. if you need to switch between unidirectional and bidirectional processing, adjust the corresponding parameters according to the processing mode. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.

en-83: caution – use of controls or adjustments or performance of procedures other than those specified here in may result in hazardous laser radiation exposure. before starting cleaning and maintenance work always switch off the device and unplug the mains plug. always keep the system clean, as flammable parts in the working area or exhaust area rise the fire hazard. you should check at least once a day, whether dust has accumulated in the engraving system. in case of soiling the machine must be cleaned. the cleaning interval strongly depends on the material that is being processed and the operating time of the device. please bear in mind that only a clean machine guarantees optimal performance and reduces the service costs. general cleaning notes: 1. make sure that the device is switched off and unplugged. open the protective cover. 2. move the working table into a position in which it is easiest for you to clean the surface with a window cleaning agent and paper towels. 3. thoroughly remove all loose dirt particles and deposits in the interior of the machine. 4. clean the cover of the laser tube. 5. you can clean the viewing window with a cotton cloth. do not use paper towels as they could scratch the window. 6. the laser nozzle should be cleaned regularly to prevent oil and grease buildup from obstructing the laser beam. it is recommended to clean the laser aperture every three days. 5.2 clean the optical parts these mirrors have durable multi-coating and won’ t be damaged by correct and careful cleaning. you should inspect the focus lens and the reflectors and the beam combiner according the maintenance plan. if you discover a veil of haze or dirt, you must clean them. it is suggested to clean the reflectors/lens before work every day in order to run the machine at max efficiency. please turn off the power of laser machine before cleaning the optical parts. 1.the lens and the reflectors must be cleaned carefully with a clean cotton swab or a dust-free cloth to avoid scratching the surface of the lens. 2.do not touch the lens with your hands after wiping. 3.never use a cleaning swab or a dust-free cloth twice. 5.2.1 clean the focus lens 1. take the lens out. 2. remove the coarse dust as good as possible by blowing air onto the lens surface. 3. clean the lens with the cleaner and swabs. 4. dry this side of the lens with dry cleaning swabs and repeat the cleaning process on the other side of the lens. never use a cleaning swabs twice. dust accumulated in the cleaning swabs could scratch the lens surface. 5. examine the lens. if it is still soiled, repeat the cleaning process until the lens is clean. finally, install the lens back. 5.2.2 clean the reflectors 1. remove the coarse dust as good as possible by blowing air onto the mirror surface. 2. clean the lens with the cleaner and swabs. 3. dry this side of the mirror with dry cleaning swabs and repeat the cleaning process on the other side of the mirror. never use a cleaning swabs twice. dust accumulated in the cleaning swabs could scratch the mirror surface. 4. examine the mirror. if it is still soiled, repeat the cleaning process until the lens is clean. 5.2.3 clean laser combiner 1. the laser combiner is installed in front of the first mirror. 2. remove the coarse dust as good as possible by blowing air onto the combiner surface. 3. clean the lens with the cleaner and swabs. 4. dry this side of the laser combiner with dry cleaning swabs and repeat the cleaning process on the other side of the lens. never use a cleaning swab twice. dust accumulated in the cleaning swabs could scratch the combiner surface. 5. examine the laser combiner. if it is still soiled, repeat the cleaning process until it is clean. 5.3 check the beam path after being used for a long time, the beam path might be deflective. this will reduce the efficient of the laser beam or even cause no laser beam. at this moment, you will need to re-adjust the beam path again. 5.4 clean the inside of the machine remove small pieces that fall into the work table, gears, rails, and belts with a small brush or vacuum cleaner. work area gears belt notice: if the belt is severely worn, it needs to be replaced. rails notice: it is advisable to apply some lubricating oil to the lead screw from time to time to prevent wear. exhaust port rf tube cooling fan 5.5 maintenance plan please strictly follow the maintenance instructions in this manual to maintain the machine. failure to adhere to these instructions or using incorrect maintenance methods may result in machine damage, affecting its performance and potentially voiding the warranty. daily weekly 3 months 6 months 12 months lens mirror 2 and 3 mirror 1 belts overall machine auto sensor work table exhaust fan bearing and rails vent slots (back side of the machine) interior work space
en-200: 1. getting started this guide will walk you through the essential steps required to safely set up the vertigo laser system and complete your first engraving task. whether you are a beginner or setting up a new machine, following these procedures will help ensure stable performance and reliable results from the very beginning. important safety notice always supervise the machine during operation. leaving the laser system unattended may result in safety hazards or damage to the equipment. 2. initial setup and machine preparation before performing any engraving, the machine must be properly initialized and prepared. step 1: level the machine place the machine on a flat and stable work surface. adjust the leveling feet at the bottom (near the casters) until the machine is level. you can verify this using the built-in level indicator inside the machine. step 2: connect power and start the machine connect the machine to a power source using the power cable. turn on the power switch and allow the machine to complete its startup process. during initialization, the laser head will automatically move to its default home position, typically located at the upper-left corner of the working area. 3. computer connection and engraving preparation before starting any engraving, you need to connect the machine to your computer and complete material positioning and focus adjustment. step 1: connect to your computer establish a connection between the machine and your computer using one of the following methods: usb connection network (ethernet) connection wireless (wi-fi) connection before proceeding, make sure your control software has successfully detected the machine. step 2: position the material after the machine has reset, place the material flat on the worktable. ensure it is stable and properly aligned with the working area beneath the laser head. step 3: adjust the focus adjust the height of the laser head and select the appropriate focusing method based on the material size. if your machine supports autofocus and the material size is suitable, run the autofocus function to achieve optimal precision. accurate focusing is essential for clean engraving results. 4. verifying optical alignment to maintain consistent engraving quality, it is important to ensure that the laser beam remains properly aligned throughout vertical movement. how to verify the optical path step 1: prepare the test surface apply a small piece of double-sided tape over the entrance of the third mirror (where the laser beam enters the mirror assembly). press the tape firmly along the edge so that a clear impression is formed, making it easier to determine whether the laser hits the center during testing. step 2: test at the lowest position move the laser head to its lowest working position. press the “pulse” button to create a burn mark on the tape. then slightly raise the laser head and check whether the mark is located at the center of the mirror inlet. if it is centered, no adjustment is needed. if not, fine-tune the adjustment screws on the first mirror until the mark is centered. step 3: test at the highest position without removing or moving the tape, raise the laser head to its highest working position. press the “pulse” button again to create a second mark. how to evaluate the results remove the tape and compare the two marks: center alignment : the second mark should appear near the center of the third mirror inlet, just like the first mark. overlap consistency : the two marks should overlap or be very close to each other. if the second mark is clearly offset, it indicates that the beam alignment shifts with height changes. in this case, fine-tune the adjustment screws on the second mirror until the marks are centered, preventing accuracy loss or power reduction during operation. 5. checking motion accuracy (backlash test) mechanical backlash may occur when the motion system changes direction, especially during high-speed engraving. this test ensures accurate positioning and prevents visual defects such as uneven edges or misaligned lines. option a: using makerboost open the settings menu from the top toolbar. select scan offset adjustment . read the backlash values. run the full test and review the results. if the result is correct (i.e., edges appear aligned to the naked eye), no adjustment is needed. if edges are uneven, adjust the backlash values, apply them, and repeat the test until accurate results are achieved. option b: using lightburn go to device settings . enable scan offset adjustment . follow the guided calibration process provided by the software (the procedure is essentially the same as in makerboost). if the backlash value cannot be read automatically, refer to the engraved value card included with the machine accessories. you can manually input the value and write it into the machine. 6. running your first engraving once all setup and calibration steps are complete, you can begin your first engraving task. import a simple design file into the software and start the engraving process. monitor the machine during operation to ensure smooth motion and consistent output quality. 7. final notes a proper setup process is the foundation of high-quality laser engraving. by ensuring correct initialization, alignment, and motion calibration, you can significantly reduce errors and improve overall performance. if you encounter any issues or require further assistance, please contact our technical support team for guidance.

en-208: mechanical backlash may occur when the motion system changes direction, especially during high-speed engraving. this test ensures accurate positioning and prevents visual defects such as uneven edges or misaligned lines. 1. option a: using makerboost open the settings menu from the top toolbar. select scan offset adjustment . read the backlash values. run the full test and review the results. if the result is correct (i.e., edges appear aligned to the naked eye), no adjustment is needed. if edges are uneven, adjust the backlash values, apply them, and repeat the test until accurate results are achieved. 2. option b: using lightburn go to device settings . enable scan offset adjustment . follow the guided calibration process provided by the software (the procedure is essentially the same as in makerboost). 3. note if the backlash value cannot be read automatically, refer to the engraved value card included with the machine accessories. you can manually input the value and write it into the machine.
en-207: 1. auto-focus function the fixture is capable of moving left and right. it will carry the material towards the laser head, making contact with the focusing accessory. subsequently, it will be adjusted to the appropriate focal length to ensure that an optimal distance is maintained between the material and the laser head. by using the auto focus function, users can focus quickly and accurately before cutting and engraving which saves the time of cutting and engraving and brings the better cutting engraving result. the diameter range of the processing materials for vertigo's auto-focus is 89~230mm (3.5”~9.05”). please follow the steps below to use the auto focus function: secure the workpiece on the fixture → click af button on panel. after that, the needed focus will be set automatically. important : ensure you press the auto-focus button only once per auto-focus operation. note: when using the autofocus function, be careful to avoid the workpiece hitting the laser head, otherwise you will damage the machine and the laser head! 2. manual focus function case 1: workpiece diameter smaller than the auto-focus minimum if the diameter of the workpiece to be processed (15–89 mm) is smaller than the minimum diameter supported by the auto-focus system (89 mm), manual focusing is required. 1.secure the workpiece in the fixture, ensuring it is level and stable. 2.insert the manual focusing tool along the lower surface of the laser head and align it with the edge protrusion. 3.adjust the workpiece along the f-axis until it just touches the manual focusing tool. note : use the on-screen controls to move the workpiece left or right along the f-axis. case 2: workpiece diameter larger than the auto-focus maximum if the diameter of the workpiece (230~300mm) to be processed exceeds the maximum diameter (230mm) supported by the auto-focus system, but the diameter at the clamping position remains within the allowable range of the chuck (20~230mm), manual focusing is required. 1.secure the workpiece on the fixture, ensuring it is level and stable. 2.note: the adjustment distance corresponds to the radius of the workpiece. 3.use the on-screen controls to move the workpiece to the right along the f-axis until the distance between the 0° mark on the vertigo angle marking plate and the 0 cm mark on the bottom f-axis equals the radius of the workpiece. note: 使用手动对焦功能时，请注意避免工件撞击激光头，否则会损坏机器和激光头！
en-210: if vertigo experiences pattern size compression during rotary scanning, causing the original graphics to fail to align or appear separated—such as in the example below: this issue is caused by abnormal scan pulse output. after inspection by technical personnel, it was found that the dip switch (sw) settings on the motor driver were incorrect. this resulted in dual pulse output, which conflicted with the pulse mode of the mainboard. the incorrect signals were then sent to the motor, causing deviations between the actual motion path and the intended trajectory. to resolve this issue, you need to remove the back panel of the vertigo: locate the motor driver sw14 switch, and adjust the switch back to the correct position as shown in the diagram: after restarting the machine, try the scanning process again—the engraving should return to normal and achieve the expected results.
en-203: proper maintenance is essential to ensure stable performance, extend the lifespan of your machine, and maintain high engraving quality. this section outlines the recommended cleaning procedures and inspection routines. 1. cleaning the laser machine safety notice improper operation, adjustments, or procedures not specified in this manual may result in hazardous laser radiation exposure. before performing any cleaning or maintenance: switch off the machine unplug the power supply a clean machine is critical for safe operation. dust and flammable debris in the working or exhaust areas can significantly increase the risk of fire. cleaning frequency the machine should be inspected at least once per day for dust accumulation. cleaning frequency depends on: material type operating time regular cleaning ensures optimal performance and reduces long-term maintenance costs. general cleaning procedure ensure the machine is powered off and unplugged. open the protective cover. move the worktable to a convenient position for cleaning. use a suitable cleaning agent (e.g., window cleaner) and paper towels to clean accessible surfaces. remove all loose debris, dust, and residues from the interior of the machine. clean the protective cover of the laser tube. clean the viewing window using a soft cotton cloth. avoid paper towels, as they may scratch the surface. clean the laser nozzle regularly to prevent oil and debris buildup that may obstruct the laser beam. recommended interval: every 3 days 2. cleaning optical components the optical components (lenses, mirrors, and beam combiner) are coated with durable multi-layer coatings. however, improper cleaning can still cause damage. general guidelines always power off the machine before cleaning inspect optical components regularly according to the maintenance schedule clean immediately if haze, dust, or contamination is observed for best performance, clean optical components daily before operation cleaning rules use only clean cotton swabs or lint-free cloths clean gently to avoid scratching optical surfaces do not touch optical surfaces with bare hands never reuse a swab or cloth (trapped dust can scratch surfaces) 2.1 cleaning the focus lens remove the lens from its mount use clean air to blow off loose dust particles gently clean the lens using an appropriate optical cleaner and a fresh swab dry the surface with a clean, dry swab repeat the process on the opposite side using new swabs inspect the lens if contamination remains, repeat the process reinstall the lens once it is completely clean 2.2 cleaning the reflectors (mirrors) blow off loose dust from the mirror surface using clean air clean the surface using optical cleaner and a fresh swab dry with a new swab repeat for the opposite side (if applicable) inspect the mirror and repeat cleaning if necessary 2.3 cleaning the beam combiner the beam combiner is located in front of the first mirror. blow off loose dust using clean air clean the surface with optical cleaner and a fresh swab dry using a clean swab repeat on the opposite side inspect and repeat cleaning if required 3. beam path inspection over time, the laser beam path may shift due to mechanical or thermal factors. misalignment can lead to: reduced efficiency decreased engraving quality complete loss of laser output if any of these issues occur, the beam path must be realigned. 4. cleaning the machine interior debris may accumulate in mechanical components during operation. regular cleaning prevents wear and ensures smooth motion. key areas to clean work area : remove leftover material and debris gears : clean dust buildup to maintain smooth transmission belts : remove debris and inspect for wear replace if severely worn rails and lead screws : remove dust and apply lubricant periodically to prevent wear exhaust port : ensure airflow is unobstructed cooling fan (rf tube) : keep clean to maintain proper cooling use a soft brush or vacuum cleaner to remove debris from these components. 5. maintenance schedule follow the maintenance schedule strictly to ensure reliable operation. improper maintenance or neglect may lead to machine damage and could void the warranty. recommended maintenance intervals daily weekly 3 months 6 months 12 months lens mirror 2 and 3 mirror 1 belts overall machine auto sensor work table exhaust fan bearing and rails vent slots (back side of the machine) interior work space additional areas to monitor： ventilation slots (rear of the machine) interior workspace cleanliness 6. final note consistent and proper maintenance is key to achieving long-term reliability and high-quality engraving results. by keeping the machine clean and following the recommended inspection schedule, you can minimize downtime, reduce repair costs, and ensure optimal performance.

en-125: this article provides an overview of the installation, configuration, and calibration procedures for using an external rotary axis on one laser x series, xt series, and xrf models. the rotary axis enables cylindrical engraving, such as on tumblers, bottles, pens, and other round objects. proper installation and calibration are essential to ensure accurate rotation and consistent engraving quality. 1. prerequisites the external rotary axis must be used together with the lifting base . before installing the rotary device, ensure that the lifting base has been fully assembled and secured. 2. installing the rotary axis step 1: remove the honeycomb panel remove the honeycomb bed from the working table to make room for the rotary attachment. step 2: position the tray and rotary axis adjust the tray height so that the laser head is approximately 3–5 cm above the surface of the workpiece. place the rotary axis onto the tray. step 3: connect the rotary axis align the groove on the rotary plug with the protrusion on the machine port . insert the connector and tighten the securing screw to ensure a stable connection. step 4: load and secure the material place the cylindrical material on the rotary rollers or chuck. turn the red knob to clamp and secure the object firmly in place. step 5: focus the laser move the laser head until the red-dot pointer aligns with the desired starting point. perform auto-focus, then switch on the rotary axis using the boat-style switch. 3. using the rotary axis in rdworks rdworks requires manual calibration to ensure the rotational steps correspond accurately to real-world motion. step 1: draw a calibration shape create a square in rdworks. click download to send the test file to the machine. measure the engraved boundary length. step 2: adjust the step value click output. turn on enable rotate engrave. if the measured dimension differs from the set value: measured value larger than set value : decrease the circle pulse (less rotation per step). measured value smaller than set value : increase the circle pulse (more rotation per step). click write. re-download the file to the machine for testing. repeat the above adjustment steps until the measured value is identical to the set value. step 3: set origin and run boundary upload the job, set the origin, run the frame check, and begin engraving. after use: restore original settings when rotary processing is finished: reopen output. turn off enable rotate engrave. the machine display will show starting program. turn off the hardware switch that connects the rotating shaft to the machine. click confirm and move on the machine display. wait until the laser head has completed its reset process. 4. using the rotary axis in lightburn lightburn provides a more guided workflow for rotary calibration. step 1: enable rotary mode navigate to laser tools. select rotary setup. turn on enable rotary. input the object diameter in the rotary settings. confirm with ok. step 2: draw a calibration shape create a square in lightburn. click send to send the test file to the machine. measure the engraved boundary length. step 3: adjust the step value if the measured dimension differs from the set value: measured value larger than set value : decrease the steps per rotation (less rotation per step). measured value smaller than set value : increase the steps per rotation (more rotation per step). continue the adjustment until the measured value is identical to the set value. step 4: start the job upload the file, set the origin, run the frame boundary, and begin engraving. after use: restore original settings when rotary processing is finished: reopen laser tools - rotary setup. turn off enable rotary. confirm with ok. the machine display will show starting program. turn off the hardware switch that connects the rotating shaft to the machine. click confirm and move on the machine display. wait until the laser head has completed its reset process. 5. summary the rotary axis extends the capabilities of one laser devices by allowing precise cylindrical engraving. proper installation, correct focusing, and accurate calibration—especially step-value tuning in rdworks or axis calibration in lightburn—are essential for predictable results. users should always restore original machine settings after rotary use to maintain normal flat-surface processing behavior.
en-277: problem description after using the rotary attachment on the xrf, the y-axis may not move as expected when switching back to normal engraving. the movement distance or step distance may also be incorrect, affecting the machine's positioning accuracy. cause the rotary mode setting in lightburn may still be enabled. when rotary mode is active, the y-axis movement is adjusted to accommodate the rotary attachment. if the machine returns to normal engraving without properly resetting its operating state, y-axis movement or step distance may be abnormal. solution open lightburn and go to tools > rotary setup . uncheck enable rotary to disable rotary mode. press the reset button on the machine's control panel, or restart the machine. run a test to confirm that the y-axis movement and step distance have returned to normal. note: after using the rotary attachment, make sure to disable rotary mode and reset or restart the machine before returning to normal engraving. if the issue persists, check the machine's settings and contact technical support if necessary. important reminder: if these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on zoho: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket . a technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
en-86: the auto feeder is a modular accessory intended to automate material feed into a primary processing machine. the assembly process is straightforward and designed so that a single operator can complete it with commonly available hand tools. notes: assembly instructions can be found in this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lob4ufa0f6e&t=32s parts & hardware prepare and identify all components 1. open the packaging of all components and place them on a clean work surface. 2. identify all parts shown in the manual: user manual conveyor rail (front) conveyor rail (rear) conveyor rail support feeding accessory main unit conveyor rail support pad l-wrench screws m5*14 screws m5*20 screws m3*8 screws m3*10 tray (removable) assembly — step-by-step for a more detailed installation guide, please refer to the youtube video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lob4ufa0f6e case 1: cutting materials with a thickness of 0 mm < h ≤ 8 mm (without spacers) step 1 - adjust base plate position 1. remove the honeycomb panel. pull out the xrf/xt base plate. 2. reinsert the third or lower placement layer from the top, which assists in the installation of the feeding accessory. step 2 - place the feeding accessory main unit 1. pull out the base plate approximately 10cm from the front corner bracket. 2. place the feeding accessory main unit. caution: there are two locations where riser blocks can be installed when assembling the auto feeder: at the feeding accessory main unit: installing the riser blocks increases the feeding clearance, allowing the auto feeder to accommodate thicker materials. at the bottom of the conveyor rail support bracket: installing the riser blocks raises the height of the roller assembly to align it with the machine. the riser blocks at these two locations cannot be used at the same time. installing both sets will result in a height mismatch and prevent proper assembly. choose one installation location based on your application and follow the corresponding installation steps. step 3 - install the feeding accessory main unit 1. align the feeding accessory main unit with the corresponding holes on the equipment, as shown in "step 3". 2. tighten the screws in the corresponding positions using m5*14 hex socket screws. step 4 - assemble the conveyor rails 1. push and insert the conveyor rail support bracket to assemble it.secure the conveyor rail support bracket using m3*8 thumb screws. 2. install the conveyor rail support bracket to the rear area of ​​the conveyor rail, paying attention to the installation direction. 3. assemble at least four conveyor rails in sequence. steps 5 & 6 - install the conveyor rails 1. pull out the base plate. 2. snap the assembled conveyor rails into the corresponding positions on the front of the feeding accessory main unit. the distance between the conveyor rails can be adjusted according to the width of the material being processed. 3. tighten the screws using m3*10 screws to secure the conveyor rails to their positions on the feeding accessory main unit. steps 7 & 8 - installing conveyor rails 1. align the corresponding holes of the new conveyor rail with the already installed one. 2. tighten the new conveyor rail using m3*10 thumb screws. 3. conveyor rails can also be installed or added to the rear of the feeding accessory main unit using the same method. before installation, use cable ties to tidy up the exhaust pipe. 4. the width between the conveyor rails on both sides of the front and rear of the feeding accessory main unit must be consistent. step 9 - connecting the feeding accessory main unit and equipment 1. connect the feeding accessory main unit and equipment, tightening the interface. 2. pay attention to the placement of the motor cables to prevent them from interfering with material processing. the recommended setup is shown in the figure below: step 10 - completing assembly 1. as shown in step 10, assembly is complete. case 2: cutting materials with a thickness of 8 mm < h ≤ 14 mm (with spacers) step 1 - adjust base plate position 1. remove the honeycomb panel. pull out the xrf/xt base plate. 2. reinsert the fourth or lower placement layer from the top, which assists in the installation of the feeding accessory. step 2 - place the feeding accessory main unit 1. install the two riser blocks on both sides of the feeding accessory main unit using m3*8 hex socket screws. 2. pull out the base plate approximately 10cm from the front corner bracket. 3. place the feeding accessory main unit. caution: there are two locations where riser blocks can be installed when assembling the auto feeder: at the feeding accessory main unit: installing the riser blocks increases the feeding clearance, allowing the auto feeder to accommodate thicker materials. at the bottom of the conveyor rail support bracket: installing the riser blocks raises the height of the roller assembly to align it with the machine. the riser blocks at these two locations cannot be used at the same time. installing both sets will result in a height mismatch and prevent proper assembly. choose one installation location based on your application and follow the corresponding installation steps. step 3 - install the feeding accessory main unit 1. align the feeding accessory main unit with the corresponding holes on the equipment, as shown in "step 3". 2. tighten the screws in the corresponding positions using m5*20 hex socket screws. step 4 - assemble the conveyor rails 1. push and insert the conveyor rail support bracket to assemble it.secure the conveyor rail support bracket using m3*8 thumb screws. 2. install the conveyor rail support bracket to the rear area of ​​the conveyor rail, paying attention to the installation direction. 3. assemble at least four conveyor rails in sequence. steps 5 & 6 - install the conveyor rails 1. pull out the base plate. 2. snap the assembled conveyor rails into the corresponding positions on the front of the feeding accessory main unit.

en-97: the onelaser riser base is a structural accessory designed to elevate a laser machine, creating additional clearance and enabling thicker workpieces or specialized fixtures. the riser base is assembled from a collection of sheet-metal panels, support brackets, reinforcing plates, and connecting strips. the manual presents labeled components (a-q; 1-6) together with eight major assembly steps. prepare and identify all components open the packaging of all components and place them on a clean work surface. identify all components shown in the manual: a~q: ● (a) left rear support ● (b) left front support ● (c) right rear support ● (d) right front support ● (e) left side panel ● (f) right side panel ● (g) left tray support plate ● (h) right tray support plate ● (i) left connecting strip ● (j) right connecting strip ● (k) rear panel ● (l) front panel ● (m) rear connecting strip ● (n) front connecting strip ● (o) reinforcing strip a ● (p) reinforcing strip b ● (q) reinforcing plate 1~6: ● flat head hex socket head cap screw m3*8 (×10) ● flat head hex socket head cap screw m4*10 (×20) ● cylindrical head hex socket head cap screw m3*8 (×8) ● cylindrical head hex socket head cap screw m4*8 (×8) ● cylindrical head hex socket head cap screw m4*10 (×6) ● cylindrical head hex socket head cap screw m4*12 (×8) ● wrench (×3) 3. refer to the diagram to confirm the orientation of the panel and structural components. assembly — step-by-step instructions step 1 - assemble the left and right pallet support plates use m3*8 (×10) flathead hex screws and a suitable wrench. assemble the left pallet support plate with the left connecting strip, and the right pallet support plate with the right connecting strip. step 2 - assemble the left panel and support components use m4*8 (×4) socket head cap screws and a suitable wrench. assemble the left panel with the left front and rear support components. step 3 - assemble the left panel and left pallet support plate use m4*10 (×10) flat head hex screws and a suitable wrench. assemble the assembled left panel assembly with the left pallet support plate. step 4 - assemble the right side panel and support components use m4*8 (×4) socket head cap screws and a suitable wrench. assemble the right side panel with the front and rear right side support components. step 5 - assemble the right side panel and right tray support plate use m4*10 (×10) flat head hex screws and a suitable wrench. assemble the assembled right side panel with the right tray support plate. step 6 - assemble the reinforcing plate and reinforcing strips use m4*10 (×6) socket head cap screws and a suitable wrench. assemble the reinforcing plate with reinforcing strips a and b. step 7 - assemble the overall frame use m4*12 (×8) socket head cap screws and a suitable wrench. assemble the previously assembled left and right side components, reinforcing plate, and front and rear panels according to the diagram. step 8 - assemble the front and rear connecting strips use m3*8 (×8) socket head cap screws and a suitable wrench. assemble the front and rear connecting strips in the corresponding positions on the top of the front and rear panels, as shown in the diagram. assembly complete! final check — assembly completed verify all screws are tightened. confirm that all panels are flush and that the riser base stands level. confirm tray support alignment. safety & best practices assemble on a flat surface to ensure correct alignment. do not fully tighten screws until all major parts are hooked in place. handle sheet-metal edges carefully to avoid cuts. after assembly, check for any resonant wobble and re-tighten connections. troubleshooting panel does not align: → loosen surrounding screws, realign, re-tighten. tray support uneven: → reinstall g and h plates, ensure horizontal alignment before tightening. base feels unstable: → check reinforcing strips o, p, and the q plate.

en-55: 2.1 general safety information all personnel involved in installation, set-up, operation maintenance and repair of the machine, must have read and understood the operation manual and in particular the "safety" section. the user is recommended to generate company-internal instructions considering the professional qualifications of the personnel employed in each case, and the receipt trained and authorized personnel. the scopes of competence for the different activities in the scope of operating the machine must be clearly defined and observed, so that under the aspect of safety no unclear questions of competence occur. this applies in particular to activities on the electric equipment, which must only be performed by special experts. for all activities concerning installation, set-up, start-up, operation, modifications of conditions and methods of operation, maintenance, inspection and repair, the switch-off procedures that may be provided in the operation manual must be observed. safety information for the user and/or operating personnel 1. no working methods are permitted that affect the safety of the machine. 2. the operator must also ensure that no unauthorized persons work with the machine. 3. it is the duty of the operator to check the machine for visible damage before use and report anything affecting safety. 4. the machine must be operated only in perfect condition. 5. keep the area around the machine clean and accessible. 6. safety components must not be removed or disabled. 7. preparation and maintenance must only be performed with equipment switched off. 8. unauthorized modifications can void the warranty. 2.2 laser safety information 1. onelaser hydra series is a class 2 device with protective housing and safety installations. please note improper operation may override safety protections. 2. the system contains a class 4 co2 laser emitting intense, invisible radiation. 3. risks without safety precautions: eyes: burns skin: burns clothing: fire hazard 4. never modify or disassemble the laser. 5. using unapproved equipment or methods may cause dangerous exposure. 2.3 safety precautions when operating the device your onelaser hydra series stops the job automatically when the lid is opened. press "pause" before interrupting a job. please remember the following safety precautions: 1. co2 fire extinguishers should be placed near the laser. 2. remove flammable materials from inside the machine. 3. maintain free airflow around the machine. 4. do not leave the machine unattended while operating. 5. always use air assist when vector cutting. 1. wear safety glasses when maintaining the machine. 2. beam path adjustments must only be made by trained personnel. 1. do not disable safety features or limit switches. 2. verify materials do not generate harmful substances and filtration is adequate. 3. never process pvc with the laser. 2.4 warning and information labels warning labels must be read and replaced immediately if damaged.
en-56: 3.1 exhaust system – requirements proper fume extraction is imperative to evacuate the combustible and noxious fumes that are created during the lasing process. this machine must be equipped with an adequate exhaust system. this includes a blower of rated flow, volume, and duty cycle as well as properly installed ducting and peripherals. you can further reduce smells from fine particulate matter with an inline filtering system. do not start the machine without an adequate exhaust system. 3.2 air system – requirements the included air pump supplies the dual stage air assist control and is a critical component. this helps keep the focusing lens clean and cool during the engraving process. air assist is also critical when cutting to reduce flame-ups and clear the debris field. always use the system’s air assist feature when vector cutting. 3.3 water cooling system – requirements we supply genuine s&a cw-5000 series active water chillers to keep the laser tube cool. overheating severely shortens tube life and causes irreparable damage to the tube. the supplied chiller only cools so it is of utmost importance to keep your laser from freezing! do not run the machine without an adequate water cooling system. 3.4 computer – requirements the following recommendation represents the minimum requirements. when using a more powerful computer the graphics are generated and displayed faster and the computing times and the data transfer to the laser are reduced. to use the newest software version, you might have to abide other requirements. • windows 11 (32 bit or 64 bit ) • windows 10 (32 bit or 64 bit ) • windows 8 (32 bit or 64 bit ) • windows 7 (32 bit or 64 bit ) windows vista (with service pack 1 or later) windows xp (with service pack 2 or later) • 1024 mb of outlet and put the other side of the pipe outside where you work (if the machine is far from the outside of the room that the gas manufactured by the machine cannot be discharged; then you might need and dust/fume filter, it can keep the air quality of your working environment well). please refer to the following pictures about how to install the exhaust pipe: 3.5.5 connecting the cooling system ① open the toolbox, and then take out the water pipes, water-error signal cable and chiller power cable. ② one of the water pipes, please connect to the water chiller where marked as “outlet”, the other en-58: 5.1 cleaning the laser machine caution – use of controls or adjustments or performance of procedures other than those specified here in may result in hazardous laser radiation exposure. before starting cleaning and maintenance work always switch off the device and unplug the mains plug. always keep the system clean, as flammable parts in the working area or exhaust area rise the fire hazard. you should check at least once a day, whether dust has accumulated in the engraving system. in case of soiling the machine must be cleaned. the cleaning interval strongly depends on the material that is being processed and the operating time of the device. please bear in mind that only a clean machine guarantees optimal performance and reduces the service costs. general cleaning notes: 1. make sure, that the device is switched off and unplugged. open the protective cover. 2. move the working table into a position in which it is easiest for you to clean the surface with a window cleaning agent and paper towels. 3. thoroughly remove all loose dirt particles and deposits in the interior of the machine. 4. clean the cover of the laser tube. 5. you can clean the viewing window with a cotton cloth. do not use paper towels as they could scratch the acrylic. 6. the laser nozzle should be cleaned regularly to prevent oil and grease buildup from obstructing the laser beam. it is recommended to clean the laser aperture every three days. 5.2 cleaning the optical parts the lens has a durable multi-coating and won’t be damaged by correct and careful cleaning. you should inspect the focus lens and the mirrors and the beam combiner according the maintenance plan. if you discover a veil of haze or dirt, you must clean them. it is suggested to clean the mirrors/lens before work every day in order to run the machine at max efficiency. please turn off the power of laser machine before cleaning the optical parts. 1. the cleaner and cotton swabs are in the tool box that came with the machine. 2. the lens must be cleaned carefully with a clean cotton swab to avoid scratching the surface of the lens. 3. do not touch the lens with your hands after wiping. 4. never use a cleaning swab twice. follow the instructions below for the cleaning of optical parts: 5.2.1 cleaning the focus lens 1. move the working head into the center of the working surface. 2. take the lens out. 3. remove the coarse dust as good as possible by blowing air onto the lens surface. 4. clean the lens with the cleaner and swabs. 5. finally, dry this side of the lens with dry cleaning swabs and repeat the cleaning process on the other side of the lens. never use a cleaning swabs twice. dust accumulated in the cleaning swabs could scratch the lens surface. 6. examine the lens. if it is still soiled, repeat the cleaning process until the lens is clean. 7. install the lens back. 5.2.2 cleaning the mirrors there are three mirrors in the operating area of the laser, which may have to be cleaned if they are soiled. to clean the reflector, follow the instructions below. 1. remove the coarse dust as good as possible by blowing air onto the mirror surface. 2. clean the lens with the cleaner and swabs. 3. finally, dry this side of the mirror with dry cleaning swabs and repeat the cleaning process on the other side of the mirror. never use a cleaning swabs twice. dust accumulated in the cleaning swabs could scratch the mirror surface. 4. examine the mirror. if it is still soiled, repeat the cleaning process until the lens is clean. 5.2.3 cleaning laser combiner 1. the laser combiner is installed on the left side of the first mirror. 2. remove the coarse dust as good as possible by blowing air onto the combiner surface. 3. clean the lens with the cleaner and swabs. 4. finally, dry this side of the laser combiner with dry cleaning swabs and repeat the cleaning process on the other side of the lens. never use a cleaning swab twice. dust accumulated in the cleaning swabs could scratch the combiner surface. 5. examine the laser combiner. if it is still soiled, repeat the cleaning process until it is clean. 5.3 check the beam path after being used for a long time, the beam path might be deflective. this will reduce the efficient of the laser beam or even cause no laser beam. at this moment, you will need to re-adjust the beam path again. 5.4 cleaning the inside of the machine remove small pieces that fall into the work table, gears, rails, and belts with a small brush or vacuum cleaner. work table gears belt rails note: can be maintained with lubricant oil. exhaust port rf tube cooling fan 5.5 clean the chiller change the pure (distilled) water of the chiller every 3 months and clean the filters. use the air blow gun to blow away the dust. 5.6 clean the exhaust fan clean the air intake. 5.7 maintenance plan please strictly follow the maintenance instructions in this manual to maintain the equipment. failure to adhere to these instructions or using incorrect maintenance methods may result in equipment damage, affecting its performance and potentially voiding the warranty. daily weekly 3 months 6 months 12 months en-94: acrylic (pmma) is one of the most laser-friendly materials available. it engraves cleanly, cuts smoothly, and produces polished edges—especially when processed with a co₂ laser, which acrylic naturally absorbs at 10.6 µm. however, beginners often get confused when choosing between cast and extruded acrylic. although they look identical, their engraving and cutting behavior is noticeably different. this guide explains how acrylic interacts with laser energy, the differences between cast and extruded types, and how to choose the right one for your project. 1. how acrylic reacts to co₂ laser processing acrylic is a clear thermoplastic with high optical transmission and excellent absorption of co₂ infrared light. when the laser beam hits the surface: for engraving: the beam vaporizes a thin layer, producing contrast or texture. for cutting: the beam melts and vaporizes material through the full thickness, forming a smooth, flame-polished edge. 2. cast vs. extruded acrylic: the essentials although both are made of pmma, the manufacturing method creates different internal structures: cast acrylic low internal stress, more uniform structure engraves with a bright, frosted white finish produces polished, glossy cut edges slightly slower cutting speed higher cost extruded acrylic higher internal stress, directionally aligned engravings appear clear, glossy, or slightly melted cuts faster and more efficiently softer edges that can deform under heat more economical in practical use: cast acrylic is preferred for engraving quality . extruded acrylic is preferred for cutting efficiency . 3. engraving acrylic: what to expect cast acrylic produces high-contrast frosted results, ideal for awards, signage, photos, and detailed graphics. extruded acrylic engraves with little to no contrast, and can melt if overheated, making it less suited for decorative or text-heavy designs. general co₂ engraving settings: cast surface engraving: 15–25% power, high speed deep engraving: 25–40% power extruded engraving: even lower power to avoid melting tip: slight positive defocus (+1 mm) can produce a cleaner white frost on cast acrylic. 4. cutting acrylic: edge quality and speed both cast and extruded acrylic cut well, but results vary: cast acrylic slower but yields the best polished, glass-like edges ideal for display panels, led signage, decorative shapes extruded acrylic cuts faster at the same power edges are smooth but may show softening or slight melting good for prototypes and cost-sensitive production general co₂ cutting guidelines: 3 mm: ~40–50% power 5 mm: ~60–70% power 8–10 mm: ~80–100% power tip: higher frequency with lower air assist gives clearer, flame-like edges. 5. practical tips for best results keep protective film on during cutting to reduce smoke stains. always engrave before cutting to avoid heat-warping engraved areas. use low-pressure air assist for engraving; medium for cutting. clean afterward with mild soap or alcohol. for matte texture, lightly sand before engraving. do not stack sheets—reflected heat can cause distortion. 6. where acrylic laser work excels acrylic is widely used across design, manufacturing, and creative industries: illuminated signs and branding awards and trophies led edge-lit panels architectural models panels, displays, and custom product parts art pieces, coasters, decorative items 7. faq q: which acrylic is better for engraving? a: cast acrylic — produces bright, frosted engravings. q: which acrylic is better for cutting? a: extruded acrylic — faster, smoother cutting. q: why does my engraving look melted? a: too much power or too slow speed; reduce energy density. q: can i engrave and cut on the same piece? a: yes — always engrave first, cut second. q: what power is suitable for 5 mm acrylic? a: 40–60w co₂ laser is sufficient for clean cuts. conclusion: which acrylic should you choose? if your goal is beautiful engraved contrast , choose cast acrylic . if your goal is efficient and fast cutting , choose extruded acrylic . both materials perform exceptionally well on a quality co₂ laser system, provided the correct settings are used. understanding your acrylic type—and adjusting parameters accordingly—is the key to producing clean, professional-grade results every time.
en-100: leather has long been valued for its craftsmanship, durability, and timeless aesthetic. today, laser technology has transformed how makers, designers, and small businesses customize and manufacture leather goods. laser cutting allows precise shapes without fraying, while laser engraving enables intricate personalization—from logos to textures. this guide provides a clear overview of how lasers interact with leather, how to choose the right materials and laser types, and how to troubleshoot common issues. 1. why lasers work well with leather laser systems (especially co₂ lasers) offer accuracy and consistency that traditional leather tools cannot match. key advantages: • contactless processing avoids tool wear and deformation • consistent repeatability for production runs • suitable for cutting, engraving, and perforation • works for both artistic designs and industrial workflow applications include wallets, belts, custom branding, packaging, accessories, and decorative products. image suggestion : a simple comparison photo showing hand-cut leather edges vs. laser-cut edges (cleaner, sealed outline). 2. how lasers interact with leather laser processing works through concentrated thermal energy. when the beam contacts leather, it vaporizes or carbonizes the surface, producing clean cuts or engraved marks. material responsiveness varies: • vegetable-tanned leather — engraves cleanly with rich contrast • chrome-tanned leather — emits stronger odor; requires better ventilation • synthetic/pvc leather — may release harmful gases; use only laser-safe materials main laser parameters: • power — depth and burn tone • speed — exposure time • frequency — smoothness of cut edges image suggestion : a diagram showing low/medium/high laser power penetration into layered leather fibers. 3. choosing the right laser type different lasers produce different effects depending on leather composition. laser type | best for | notes co₂ laser (10.6 μm) | cutting & engraving natural leathers | smooth edges, slight darkening fiber laser (1064 nm) | marking coated or synthetic leather | precise surface marking; limited depth diode laser (455 nm) | light engraving on thin leathers | slower; requires multiple passes for most leather cutting and engraving, co₂ lasers deliver the best overall results. image suggestion : side-by-side engraving samples from co₂, fiber, and diode lasers on the same leather. 4. cutting leather: precision, clean edges, and techniques laser cutting offers unmatched accuracy, especially on curves or perforations. how to improve cut quality: • use air assist to minimize smoke and char • apply masking tape to reduce burn marks • increase speed or reduce power to avoid dark edges • test settings on scrap pieces vegetable-tanned leather generally yields the best edges. image suggestion : cross-section comparison of edges cut at different speeds and air-assist levels. 5. engraving leather: depth, texture, and style laser engraving adds detail or personalization onto the leather surface. engraving styles: surface marking — light, subtle tone change deep engraving — textured recess like an embossed finish vector engraving — thin line work suitable for illustrations control engraving depth through power, speed, and focus distance. slightly defocusing the beam can soften the engraving. typical uses: • monograms, initials • journal covers • custom fashion pieces • corporate branding image suggestion : a visual chart showing shallow vs. deep engravings with different textures (grid, lines, patterns). 6. leather material types: what is safe and what to avoid material safety and finish depend heavily on composition. type | laser suitability | notes genuine leather | excellent | natural smell; consistent finish vegetable-tanned | best | clean engraving; safe to process chrome-tanned | caution | requires strong ventilation pvc leather | unsafe | may release chlorine gas pu faux leather | limited | results vary; always test first always verify material labels before processing synthetic leathers. image suggestion : a safety infographic indicating “safe / caution / avoid” categories for leather materials. 7. finishing and post-processing post-processing improves both appearance and durability. cleaning: • brush away residue • use alcohol wipes for soot • blow off dust with low-pressure air enhancement: • apply leather conditioner for sheen • seal cut edges with wax or edge paint • add color into engraved areas for contrast image suggestion : before-and-after comparison of engraved leather before cleaning and after finishing. 8. design ideas and applications popular creative and commercial uses: • wallets, belts, keychains • book covers, laptop sleeves • custom branding and corporate gifts • leather furniture accents • home décor and wall art image suggestion : collage of leather items featuring laser engraving and cutting. 9. common problems and troubleshooting problem | cause | solution burned edges | excess power, slow speed | lower power; increase speed uneven engraving | incorrect focus height | re-adjust z-axis smoke stains | low air assist | increase airflow; apply masking sticky residue | overheating | clean with alcohol wipe image suggestion : troubleshooting chart with icons illustrating each issue. 10. frequently asked questions q: can all leather be laser-cut? a: no. use vegetable-tanned or verified natural leather; avoid pvc. q: why does engraved leather smell? a: it results from burned organic fibers; improve ventilation. q: how to reduce burn marks? a: add masking film, lower power, or increase cutting speed. q: best laser type for small workshops? a: a 40–100w co₂ laser balances cost, speed, and precision. q: can engraving be combined with embossing? a: yes. many designers use laser engraving for detail and embossing for tactile features. 11. practice recommendations • test engraving on different leather types • try varying power/speed to control burn depth • practice stitching-simulation textur
